Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 10, verse 1–2:

Tafsir of Surah Yunus

[It is Makki] [[Addition from MS T.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

As for the disjoined letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) at the beginnings of the surahs, the discussion of them has already preceded in full [[Addition from MS T, A.]] at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah.

Abu al-Duha related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the words of the Exalted, "Alif-Lam-Ra," that it means: "I am Allah, the All-Seeing." Likewise said al-Dahhak and others.

﴿These are the verses of the Wise Book﴾, that is: these are the verses of the Qur'an, the firm and clear. Mujahid said: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book﴾ [He said: the Torah and the Gospel] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Tabari (15/11), drawn from the Dar al-Sha'b edition.]]

[al-Hasan said: the Torah and the Psalms] [[Addition from MS T, A.]]

Qatadah said concerning ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾: it refers to the books that came before the Qur'an.

I do not know the meaning or the basis of this statement.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind that We revealed to a man from among them, "Warn mankind and give good tidings to those who believe"?﴾ and so on, the Exalted is rebuking those among the disbelievers who marvelled at the sending of messengers from among mankind, just as He related about the earlier generations their saying: ﴿Are mere humans guiding us?﴾ [At-Taghabun: 6]. Hud and Salih said to their peoples: ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you?﴾ [Al-A'raf: 63, 69]. And the Exalted related about the disbelievers of Quraysh that they said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is an astonishing thing!﴾ [Sad: 5].

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: When Allah the Exalted sent Muhammad (ﷺ) as a messenger, the Arabs denied that, or those among them who denied it said: "Allah is greater than that His messenger should be a human like Muhammad." He said: Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿Is it a wonder for mankind that We revealed to a man from among them﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That they have a sure standing (qadam sidq) with their Lord﴾, the scholars differed concerning it. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿That they have a sure standing with their Lord﴾ that he said: happiness had preceded for them in the Primordial Record (al-dhikr al-awwal).

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿That they have a sure standing with their Lord﴾ means: a good reward for what they had sent forward. Likewise said al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. This is like His saying: ﴿to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a goodly reward, abiding therein forever﴾ [Al-Kahf: 2-3].

Mujahid said: ﴿That they have a sure standing with their Lord﴾ means: the righteous deeds, their prayer, their fasting, their charity, and their glorification of Allah.

['Amr ibn al-Harith related from Qatadah or al-Hasan: ﴿That they have a sure standing with their Lord﴾] [[Addition from MS T.]] said: Muhammad (ﷺ) is their intercessor. Likewise said Zayd ibn Aslam and Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Qatadah said: a sound predecessor (salaf sidq) with their Lord.

Ibn Jarir preferred the view of Mujahid, that it refers to the righteous deeds they had sent forward. He said: as it is said, "He has a standing (qadam) in Islam," and from it is the saying of Hassan, may Allah be pleased with him:

We have the higher standing over you, and those after us follow our predecessors in obedience to Allah.

And the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

You have a standing that people do not deny, along with an ancient lineage that rose over the sea.

* *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The disbelievers said, "Indeed, this is clearly a sorcerer."﴾ That is: although We sent to them a messenger from among them, a man of their own kind, as a bearer of good tidings and a warner, ﴿the disbelievers said, "Indeed, this is clearly a sorcerer"﴾, that is: evident, and they were lying in that.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 10, verse 3:

He, may He be exalted, informs that He is the Lord of all the worlds, and that He created the heavens and the earth in six days. It has been said: like these days of ours; and it has been said: each day is like a thousand years of what you count, as its explanation will come, God willing. Then He istawa (rose) over the Throne, and the Throne is the greatest of the created things and its ceiling.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hajjaj ibn Hamzah narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, who said: I heard Sa'd al-Ta'i saying: "The Throne is a red ruby."

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "Allah created it from His light."

And this is gharib (strange).

﴿He manages the affair﴾, i.e., He manages the affairs of the creation, ﴿not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth escapes Him﴾ [Saba': 3], and no affair preoccupies Him from another affair, and questions do not overwhelm Him, and the insistence of those who insist does not weary Him, and the management of the great does not distract Him from the small, in the mountains, the seas, the inhabited lands and the deserts. ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah, and He knows its place of dwelling and its place of storage; all is in a clear record﴾ [Hud: 6]. ﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but it is in a clear record﴾ [al-An'am: 59].

Al-Darawardi narrated from Sa'd ibn Ishaq ibn Ka'b [ibn 'Ujrah] that he said: when this verse was revealed, ﴿Indeed your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾, a great caravan met them from among the Arabs, and they said to them: "Who are you?" They said: "From the jinn. We came out from Madinah, and this verse drove us out." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

His saying ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾ is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], and like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And how many an angel in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except after Allah permits for whom He wills and approves﴾ [al-Najm: 26], and His saying: ﴿And intercession will not benefit with Him except for one whom He has permitted﴾ [Saba': 23].

* *

His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not remember?﴾ means: single Him out for worship alone, with no partner. ﴿Will you not remember?﴾ means: O polytheists, in your affair, you worship besides Allah others, while you know that He is the sole Creator, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you asked them who created them, they would surely say, Allah﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87], and His saying: ﴿Say: Whose is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Great Throne? They will say: "Allah." Say: "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 86-87], and likewise the verse before it and the one after it.

The Most High informs that the return of all creatures is to Him on the Day of Resurrection; He leaves none of them without bringing them back as He originated them. Then He mentioned that just as He originated creation, so He will bring it back: ﴿And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [ar-Rum: 27].

﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾, i.e., with justice and the complete recompense, ﴿and those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾, i.e., because of their disbelief they will be punished on the Day of Resurrection with various kinds of retribution, from ﴿scorching wind and scalding water and a shade of black smoke﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 42, 43]. ﴿This is it, so let them taste it: scalding water and dark, foul liquid, and other punishments of similar kind﴾ [Sad: 57, 58]. ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals denied. They will go around between it and scalding water, intensely hot﴾ [ar-Rahman: 43, 44].

He, may He be exalted, informs of the signs He created that point to the perfection of His power and the greatness of His dominion. He made the light emanating from the body of the sun a radiance (ḍiyā'), and the light of the moon a light (nūr). This is one kind, and that is another kind. He differentiated between them so that they would not be confused. He made the sun's authority in the daytime and the moon's authority at night. He measured the moon into phases (manāzil): it first appears small, then its light and body increase until it becomes full and reaches its completeness (ibdār), then it begins to wane until it returns to its original state at the end of a month. As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And for the moon We have determined phases until it returns like the old dried stalk of a palm. It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outpace the day, and each is traveling in an orbit.﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 39–40]. He also said: ﴿The sun and the moon [move] by calculation. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ [al-An'ām: 96].

He said in this noble verse: ﴿and He determined it﴾, meaning the moon, ﴿and determined for it phases, that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾. Thus by the sun the days are known, and by the course of the moon the months and years are known.

﴿Allah did not create that except in truth﴾, meaning He did not create it in vain; rather, in it there is a great wisdom and a conclusive proof. As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them without purpose. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.﴾ [Ṣād: 27]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain and that you would not be returned to Us? Exalted is Allah, the True King; there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.﴾ [al-Mu'minūn: 115–116].

* *

His saying: ﴿He details the signs﴾, meaning He makes clear the proofs and evidences, ﴿for a people who know.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day﴾, meaning their succession: when this comes, that goes, and when that goes, this comes, without either delaying the other at all. As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿He covers the night over the day, which pursues it swiftly﴾ [al-A'rāf: 54]. He also said: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outpace the day﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 40]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿He is the Splitter of the dawn and has made the night for rest and the sun and moon for calculation. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾ [al-An'ām: 96].

* *

His saying: ﴿And what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning among the signs that point to His greatness, may He be exalted, as He said: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by while they turn away from it﴾ [Yūsuf: 105]. [[Addition from ت, أ, and in هـ: "the sign".]] [And He said [[in أ: "and His saying".]]: ﴿Say, "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth." But signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe.﴾ [Yūnus: 101]. [[Addition from ت, أ.]] And He said: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and behind them of the heaven and the earth?﴾ [Saba': 9]. [[In ت: "they look".]] And He said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.﴾ [Āl 'Imrān: 190]. That is, the intellects. Here He said: ﴿are signs for a people who fear Allah﴾, meaning the punishment of Allah, His wrath, and His torment.

Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, they did not adorn it, nor did they elevate it, until they became content with it while they were heedless of the signs of Allah in the cosmos, so they do not reflect upon them, and of the legislated signs, so they do not heed them, and their abode on the Day of their return is the Fire, as a recompense for what they used to earn in their worldly life of sins, transgressions and crimes, along with their disbelief in Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Day."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 10, verse 9–10:

This is an report about the state of the blessed (al-su'ada') who believed in Allah, affirmed the messengers, and complied with what they were commanded, so they did righteous deeds. [It means] that He will guide them by their faith.

It is possible that the "ba'" here is causal (sababiyyah), so the meaning is: because of their faith in the world, Allah will guide them on the Day of Resurrection over the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), until they cross it and reach Paradise. It is also possible that it is for seeking help (li'l-isti'anah), as Mujahid said regarding His words: ﴿Their Lord will guide them by their faith﴾, he said: [It will be a light for them by which they walk.]

Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words: ﴿Their Lord will guide them by their faith﴾, he said: Their deed will be presented to him in a beautiful form and a pleasant fragrance when he rises from his grave. It will meet its companion and give him good news of every good thing, and he will say to it: "Who are you?" It will say: "I am your deed." Then a light will be made for him from before him until it brings him into Paradise. That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their Lord will guide them by their faith﴾. As for the disbeliever, his deed will be presented to him in an evil form and a foul smell, so it will cling to its companion and keep hold of him until it casts him into the Fire.

Something similar was narrated from Qatadah as a mursal report, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿Their call therein will be, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and their greeting therein will be, "Peace," and the last of their call will be, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ That is: this is the state of the people of Paradise.

Ibn Jurayj said: I was informed that His saying: ﴿Their call therein, "Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾ [means]: when birds pass by them desiring them, they say: "Glory be to You, O Allah." That is their call. Then the angel comes to them with what they desire, greets them, and they return the greeting. That is His saying: ﴿and their greeting therein is "Peace."﴾ He said: When they eat, they praise Allah their Lord, and that is His saying: ﴿and the last of their call is "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: When the people of Paradise want to call for food, one of them says: "Glory be to You, O Allah." He said: Ten thousand servants stand before each one of them, with each servant a golden dish containing food not found in the others. He said: Then he eats from all of them.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: When any of them wishes to call for something, he says: "Glory be to You, O Allah."

This verse resembles His saying: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be "Peace," and He has prepared for them a noble reward﴾ [al-Ahzab: 44], and His saying: ﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk or sinful speech, except the saying "Peace, peace."﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 25–26], and His saying: ﴿"Peace," a word from a Merciful Lord﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58], and His saying: ﴿The angels will enter upon them from every gate, "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; how excellent is the final home."﴾ [al-Ra'd: 23–24].

* *

His saying: ﴿And the last of their call will be, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ This indicates that Allah, exalted is He, is the One praised forever and the One worshipped throughout all time. For this reason He praised Himself at the beginning of His creation and its continuation, at the beginning of His Book, and at the beginning of His revelation, where He says, exalted is He: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who sent down to His servant the Book﴾ [al-Kahf: 1], ﴿Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 1], and other situations too lengthy to detail. He is praised at the beginning and the end, in this worldly life and in the Hereafter, in all conditions. For this reason it came in the hadith: "The people of Paradise are inspired to glorify and praise [Allah] just as they are inspired to breathe." [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2835), from the hadith of Jabir (رضي الله عنه).] That is only so because of what they see of the multiplying of Allah's blessings upon them, so they are repeated, renewed and increased, and they have no end or limit. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

His saying: ﴿Their call therein will be, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and their greeting therein will be, "Peace," and the last of their call will be, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ That is: this is the state of the people of Paradise.

Ibn Jurayj said: I was informed that His saying: ﴿Their call therein, "Glory be to You, O Allah"﴾ [means]: when birds pass by them desiring them, they say: "Glory be to You, O Allah." That is their call. Then the angel comes to them with what they desire, greets them, and they return the greeting. That is His saying: ﴿and their greeting therein is "Peace."﴾ He said: When they eat, they praise Allah their Lord, and that is His saying: ﴿and the last of their call is "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: When the people of Paradise want to call for food, one of them says: "Glory be to You, O Allah." He said: Ten thousand servants stand before each one of them, with each servant a golden dish containing food not found in the others. He said: Then he eats from all of them.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: When any of them wishes to call for something, he says: "Glory be to You, O Allah."

This verse resembles His saying: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be "Peace," and He has prepared for them a noble reward﴾ [al-Ahzab: 44], and His saying: ﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk or sinful speech, except the saying "Peace, peace."﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 25–26], and His saying: ﴿"Peace," a word from a Merciful Lord﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58], and His saying: ﴿The angels will enter upon them from every gate, "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured; how excellent is the final home."﴾ [al-Ra'd: 23–24].

* *

His saying: ﴿And the last of their call will be, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ This indicates that Allah, exalted is He, is the One praised forever and the One worshipped throughout all time. For this reason He praised Himself at the beginning of His creation and its continuation, at the beginning of His Book, and at the beginning of His revelation, where He says, exalted is He: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who sent down to His servant the Book﴾ [al-Kahf: 1], ﴿Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 1], and other situations too lengthy to detail. He is praised at the beginning and the end, in this worldly life and in the Hereafter, in all conditions. For this reason it came in the hadith: "The people of Paradise are inspired to glorify and praise [Allah] just as they are inspired to breathe." [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2835), from the hadith of Jabir (رضي الله عنه).] That is only so because of what they see of the multiplying of Allah's blessings upon them, so they are repeated, renewed and increased, and they have no end or limit. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: He, may He be exalted, informs of His forbearance and gentleness toward His servants: that He does not answer them when they supplicate against themselves, their wealth, or their children in a state of their irritation and anger. He knows from them that they did not intend to will that. So for this reason He does not answer them in that state, out of gentleness and mercy, just as He answers them when they pray for themselves, their wealth, and their children with goodness, blessing, and increase.

Hence He says: ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good, their term would have been decreed for them.﴾ That is: if He answered them in everything they asked for in that regard, He would have destroyed them. But it is not appropriate to do this often, as came in the hadith narrated by the hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar in his Musnad:

Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Hatim ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Mujahid Abu Hazra narrated to us, from Ubada ibn al-Walid, who narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not supplicate against yourselves, do not supplicate against your children, do not supplicate against your wealth, lest you coincide with a moment from Allah in which supplication is answered, and He answers you."

Abu Dawud also narrated it, from the hadith of Hatim ibn Isma'il, with the same chain. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1532). Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, no. (3009), in a longer form, through the route of Hatim ibn Isma'il.]

Al-Bazzar said: Ubada ibn al-Walid ibn Ubada ibn al-Samit al-Ansari was alone in narrating it, and no one shared it with him. This is like His saying: ﴿And man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man has always been hasty.﴾ [al-Isra' 17:11]

Mujahid said in explaining this verse, ﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil as they seek to hasten the good﴾: it is the saying of a person to his child or his wealth when he is angry with it: "O Allah, do not bless it, and curse it." So if He hastened to answer them in that, as He answers them in good, He would have destroyed them.

Allah, exalted is He, informs us about man's impatience and anxiety when harm touches him, as in His saying: ﴿And when evil touches him, he has lengthy supplication﴾ [Fussilat: 51], meaning abundant. The two verses have the same meaning. When hardship befalls him, he becomes anxious and distressed by it, and he increases his supplication at that time. He calls upon Allah to remove it and relieve him of it while lying down, sitting, standing, and in all his conditions. But when Allah relieves his hardship and removes his distress, he turns away, goes off, and acts as if he had never been afflicted by it, ﴿Passing on as though he had never called upon Us for a harm that touched him﴾.

Then Allah, exalted is He, condemned the one who has this characteristic and this way, saying: ﴿Thus it is made attractive to the transgressors what they have been doing﴾. As for the one whom Allah grants guidance, rectitude, success, and right direction, he is excepted from this, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds﴾ [Hud: 11]. This is like the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "How wondrous is the affair of the believer! Allah does not decree for him any decree except that it is good for him. If adversity befalls him, he is patient, and it is good for him; and if ease befalls him, he is grateful, and it is good for him." And this is not the case for anyone except the believer.

[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2999), from the hadith of Suhayb al-Rumi, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Allah, exalted is He, informs us of what He brought upon the earlier generations because they denied their messengers, despite the clear signs and evident proofs that the messengers brought them. Then Allah made these people successors (khala'if) after them, and sent a messenger to them, to see (liyanzura) their obedience to Him and their following of His messenger.

In Sahih Muslim (Sahih Muslim, a collection of hadith) from the hadith of Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, this world is sweet and green, and Allah is making you successors in it, so He will see what you do. So beware of the world, and beware of women, for the first trial of the Children of Israel was with women." [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2742).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Zayd ibn Awf Abu Rabi'ah Fahd narrated to us [[In H and T: "Mahd," and in A: "Shahd"; the correction is from al-Tabari.]], Hammad narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, that Awf ibn Malik said to Abu Bakr: "I saw in what the sleeper sees as if a rope were lowered from the sky, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was pulled up by it, then it was lowered again, and Abu Bakr was pulled up by it, then people were measured around the pulpit, and Umar exceeded them by three cubits to the pulpit." Umar said: "Leave us from your dream, we have no need for it!" When Umar was made caliph, he said: "O Awf, your dream!" He said: "Do you want my dream, or have you not dismissed me?" He said: "Woe to you! I disliked that you should announce to the caliph of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ his own death!" So he related the dream to him, until he reached: "People were measured to the pulpit by these three cubits," and he said: "As for one of them, he will indeed be a caliph. As for the second, he will not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah's cause. As for the third, he is a martyr." He said: He (Awf) said: Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Then We made you successors in the land after them, that We might see how you would act﴾. So you have been made caliph, O son of Umar's mother, so look how you will act. As for his saying: "I do not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah's cause," then, what Allah wills! As for his saying: "He is a martyr," how could Umar attain martyrdom while the Muslims surround him? [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/39).]]

Ibn Kathir said:

God, exalted is He, informs us about the obstinacy of the disbelievers among the polytheists of Quraysh, who denied the truth and turned away from it: when the Messenger ﷺ recited to them the Book of God and its clear proofs, they said to him: ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this﴾, meaning: reject this and bring us something else of a different style, or change it into another form. God said to His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him: ﴿Say: It is not for me to change it on my own accord﴾, meaning: this is not up to me; I am only a servant who is commanded, and a messenger who conveys from God. ﴿I follow only what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day﴾.

Then He said, arguing against them concerning the truth of what had come to them with him: ﴿Say: Had God willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you aware of it﴾, meaning: I have brought this to you only by God's permission to me in that and by His will and His decree. The proof that I do not fabricate it from myself, nor have I invented it [in one manuscript: "uftarīhi"; in another: "aqrabahu"], is that you are unable to produce its equal, and that you know my truthfulness and trustworthiness from the time I grew up among you until God, mighty and majestic, sent me; you find no fault in me that you could reproach me with. For this reason He said: ﴿I have already lived among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then reason?﴾, meaning: do you not have minds by which you distinguish truth from falsehood?

For this reason, when Heraclius, king of the Romans, asked Abu Sufyan and those with him, among the things he asked about the attributes of the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "Did you ever accuse him of lying before he said what he said?" Abu Sufyan said: "I said: No." At that time Abu Sufyan was the head of the disbelievers and the leader of the polytheists, and yet despite this he acknowledged the truth:

"And excellence is what even the enemies testify to..."

Heraclius said to him: "I know that he would not abandon lying to people only to then go and lie about God."

Ja'far ibn Abi Talib said to al-Najashi, king of Abyssinia: "God sent among us a messenger whose lineage, truthfulness and trustworthiness we know. The period of his stay among us before prophethood was forty years." And from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: "Forty-three years." The sound and well-known view is the first.

Ibn Kathir said:

Heraclius said to him: "I know that he would not abandon lying to people only to then go and lie about God."

The period of his stay among us before prophethood was forty years." And from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: "Forty-three years." The sound and well-known view is the first.

Allah the Exalted says: There is no one more wrongful, more defiant, or more guilty ﴿than he who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾, and claims to speak on behalf of Allah, and asserts that Allah has sent him, when this is not so. There is no one greater in crime or more grievous in wrongdoing than this, and such a matter is not hidden from the foolish, so how could the state of such a person be confused with that of the prophets? Whoever makes this claim, whether truthfully or falsely, Allah will surely set up for him proofs of his righteousness or his wickedness, clearer than the sun. The difference between Muhammad (ﷺ) and Musaylimah al-Kadhdhab (may Allah curse him) is, for whoever witnessed both of them, more evident than the difference between the time of mid-morning (ḍuḥa) and the middle of the night in pitch darkness. From the marks of each of them, and from his speech and his actions, the one who has insight can deduce the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the falsehood of Musaylimah al-Kadhdhab, Sajah, and al-Aswad al-Ansi.

Abdullah ibn Salam said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, the people rushed toward him, and I was among those who rushed. When I saw him, I knew that his face was not the face of a liar. The first thing I heard him say was: "O people, spread the greeting of peace, feed the food, [maintain the ties of kinship], and pray at night while people are asleep, and you will enter Paradise in peace." (Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (5/451) and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. 2485, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.")

When Dimam ibn Thalabah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on behalf of his people, Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr, he said to the Messenger of Allah, among what he said: Who raised this sky? He said: "Allah." He said: Who set up these mountains? He said: "Allah." He said: Who spread out this earth? He said: "Allah." He said: By He who raised this sky, set up these mountains, and spread out this earth, has Allah sent you to all the people? He said: "Yes, by Allah." Then he asked him about the prayer, the zakah, the hajj, and the fasting, and at each one he swore the same oath, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) swore too. Then he said to him: "You have spoken the truth. By He who sent you with the truth, I will not add to this or subtract from it." (Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 12, from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), with a similar wording.)

This man was satisfied with this alone, and he had become certain of the truthfulness of the Messenger (ṣalawāt Allah wa salāmuhu ʿalayhi), by what he saw and witnessed of the proofs indicating it, as Hassan ibn Thabit said:

Had there been no clear signs in him,
his very presence would have brought you the news.

As for Musaylimah, whoever witnessed him from among those of insight knew his matter without doubt, through his feeble statements which are not eloquent, and his actions which are not good but rather ugly, and his Qur'an by which he will be made to abide in the Fire on the Day of Regret and Disgrace. How great is the difference between the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except for what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation does not tire Him, and He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], and the nonsense of Musaylimah, may Allah curse him and disfigure him: "O frog, daughter of two frogs, sing as you will, you neither muddy the water nor prevent the drinker." And his saying, cursed and damned: "Allah has blessed the pregnant woman, for He has brought out from her a soul that moves, from between membrane and belly." And his saying, may Allah make him abide in the fire of Hell, as he deserves: "The elephant, and what will make you know what the elephant is? It has a long trunk." And his saying, may Allah remove him far from His mercy: "By those who knead dough, and those who bake bread, and those who swallow morsels, with ghee and butter. Indeed Quraysh are a people who transgress." And other such ravings and fables, which children would be ashamed to utter except in mockery and ridicule. For this reason Allah humbled his nose, and he drank his death on the day of "Hadiqat al-Mawt," and his community was scattered. His companions and his family cursed him. They came to al-Siddiq, seeking repentance, and came to the religion of Allah willingly. Al-Siddiq, the Caliph of the Messenger (ṣalawāt Allah wa salāmuhu ʿalayhi), and may Allah be pleased with him, asked them to recite to him something of the Qur'an of Musaylimah, may Allah curse him. They asked him to excuse them from that, but he refused except that they recite some of it, so that he might let those who had not heard it from the people hear it, and they might recognize the excellence of the guidance and knowledge they were upon. So they recited to him from what we have mentioned and similar things. When they finished, al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said to them: Woe to you! Where was your intellect taken away? By Allah, this did not come out of any sound mind.

It is also reported that ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs went as an envoy to Musaylimah, and he had been a friend of his in the Jahiliyyah, and ʿAmr had not yet embraced Islam. Musaylimah said to him: Woe to you, O ʿAmr, what has been revealed to your companion, meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), during this period? He said: I heard his companions reciting a great, short surah. He said: And what is it? He said: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾ [al-ʿAsr]. Musaylimah thought for a while, then said: Something like it has also been revealed to me. He said: And what is it? He said: "O Wabr, you are only two ears and a chest, and the rest of you is a burrowing and a pecking. How do you see it, O ʿAmr?" ʿAmr said to him: "By Allah, you know that I know that you are lying." If this was the case with a polytheist in his state of polytheism, the state of Muhammad (ﷺ) was not confused for him, so he affirmed him, and the state of Musaylimah, cursed be he, so he denied him. How then about the people of insight and understanding, and the people of sound and upright minds and reason!

For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And who is more wrongful than one who fabricates a lie against Allah, or says, "It has been revealed to me," when nothing has been revealed to him, or who says, "I will reveal the like of what Allah has revealed"﴾ [al-An'am: 93], and He said in this noble verse: ﴿And who is more wrongful than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ [al-An'am: 21]. Likewise, whoever denies the truth that the messengers brought, and upon which the proofs were established, there is no one more wrongful than him, as has come in the hadith: "The most defiant of people against Allah is a man who killed a prophet, or whom a prophet killed." (Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/407) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, with the wording: "The people who will suffer the most severe punishment on the Day of Resurrection is a man whom a prophet killed or who killed a prophet." And al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4073, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "The anger of Allah intensifies against one whom the Messenger of Allah kills in the way of Allah.")

The Most High denounces the polytheists who worshipped others alongside Allah, supposing that those deities would benefit them through their intercession with Allah. So He informed them that they neither benefit, nor harm, nor possess anything, and that nothing of what they claim for them occurs, and it never will. For this reason the Most High said: ﴿Say: Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?﴾

Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] said: its meaning is, "Do you inform Allah of what does not exist in the heavens or on the earth?" Then He declared Himself exalted above their association and disbelief, saying: ﴿Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾

Then the Most High informed that this polytheism is something that arose among people, occurring after it had not existed, and that all people were upon one religion, which is Islam. Ibn Abbas said: "Between Adam and Nuh there were ten centuries, all of them upon Islam. Then differences arose among the people, and idols, rivals and images were worshipped. So Allah sent the messengers with His signs, His clear proofs, His conclusive arguments and His decisive evidences, ﴿so that whoever perishes might perish by clear evidence, and whoever lives might live by clear evidence﴾ [Al-Anfal: 42]."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And were it not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been decided between them concerning that in which they differ﴾, that means: were it not for what had already passed from Allah, the Most High, that He does not punish anyone except after the establishment of proof against him, and that He has delayed creation until a specified term, it would have been decided between them concerning that over which they differed, so that He would have made the believers happy and distressed the disbelievers.

As for His saying: ﴿And were it not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been decided between them concerning that in which they differ﴾, that means: were it not for what had already passed from Allah, the Most High, that He does not punish anyone except after the establishment of proof against him, and that He has delayed creation until a specified term, it would have been decided between them concerning that over which they differed, so that He would have made the believers happy and distressed the disbelievers.

Ibn Kathir said: That is, these disbelievers, the deniers and the obstinate ones [the heretics], say: "Why has no sign been sent down to Muhammad from his Lord?" They mean, as God gave Thamud the she-camel, or that He would turn Safa into gold for them, or remove from them the mountains of Makkah and put in their place gardens and rivers, and similar things that God is able to do. But He is wise in His actions and His words, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces﴾ [al-Furqan: 10, 11]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We send the signs only as a warning﴾ [al-Isra': 59].

He, exalted is He, says: Indeed My way with My creation is that when I give them what they ask, if they believe, well and good; otherwise I hasten the punishment upon them. For this reason, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was given the choice between being given what they asked, and then if they answered, well and good, but if not, they would be hastened upon, or leaving them and granting them respite, he chose to grant them respite, just as he bore patiently with them more than once, may the blessings of God be upon him. For this reason, God, exalted is He, said, guiding His Prophet to the answer to what they asked: ﴿Say: The unseen belongs only to God﴾, that is, the whole matter belongs to God, and He knows the outcomes of affairs, ﴿so wait; I am with you among those who wait﴾, that is: if you will not believe until you see what you asked for, then wait for the judgment of God concerning me and concerning you.

This is despite the fact that they had already witnessed from his miracles (peace be upon him) something greater than what they asked, when he pointed to the moon in their presence on the night it was full, and it split into two parts, one part behind the mountain and one part beyond it. This is greater than all the earthly signs they asked for and those they did not ask for. Had God known that they were asking for guidance and certainty, He would have answered them; but He knew that they were only asking out of obstinacy and stubbornness, so He left them in their doubt, and He knew that none of them would believe, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 96, 97]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered everything before them, they would not have believed unless God willed; but most of them are ignorant﴾ [al-An'am: 111]. And because of their arrogance, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if We opened for them a gate from the sky and they kept ascending through it, they would say: "Our eyes have only been dazzled; rather, we are a people bewitched"﴾ [al-Hijr: 14, 15]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if they saw a fragment of the sky falling, they would say: "A layered cloud"﴾ [al-Tur: 44]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if We had sent down to you a writing on paper, and they had touched it with their hands, the disbelievers would have said: "This is nothing but clear magic"﴾ [al-An'am: 7]. Such people are less deserving of being answered in what they asked, because there is no benefit in answering such people, since it revolves around their stubbornness and obstinacy, due to the abundance of their wickedness and corruption. For this reason He said: ﴿So wait; I am with you among those who wait﴾.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, the Exalted, informs that when He lets people taste mercy after a hardship that has touched them, such as ease after hardship, abundance after drought, rain after famine and the like, ﴿then they plot against Our signs﴾.

Mujahid said: "(Plotting here means) mockery and denial." This is like His saying: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing; but when We remove his harm from him, he continues on as if he had never called upon Us against a harm that touched him﴾ [Yunus: 12]. And in the Sahih it is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led them in the dawn prayer following a rain (samaʾ, meaning rain) that had fallen on them during the night. Then he said: "Do you know what your Lord said tonight?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "He said: 'In the morning some of My servants have become believers in Me and some disbelievers. As for the one who said, "We have been given rain by the grace of Allah and His mercy," he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the star. As for the one who said, "We have been given rain by such-and-such a star (nawʾ),” he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the star.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 846, and Sahih Muslim, no. 71.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Say: Allah is swifter in plotting﴾, that is, more severe in leading on (istidraj) and in granting respite, until the wrongdoer thinks that he will not be punished, and that he is only in a period of respite. Then he is seized when he is heedless. The noble recording angels write down everything he does and record it against him, and then these are presented to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, who will recompense him for the small and the great, the trivial and the most trivial, and the speck.

Then He informs that: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾, that is, He protects you and guards you with His watchfulness, ﴿until, when you are on ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it﴾, that is, in the swiftness of their journey, being favoured, ﴿then a violent wind comes upon them﴾, that is, a severe one, ﴿and the waves come at them from every place﴾, that is, the sea became rough against them, ﴿and they think they are encompassed﴾, that is, they are destroyed, ﴿they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾, that is, they do not call upon any idol or statue alongside Him, but single Him out in supplication and entreaty, as He said: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away; and man is ever ungrateful﴾ [al-Isra: 67]. And here He said: ﴿They call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion: "If You deliver us from this,"﴾, that is, this condition, ﴿"we will surely be among the thankful."﴾, that is, "We will not associate anyone with You, and we will single You out in worship there as we have singled You out in supplication here." As for His saying: ﴿The enjoyment of the life of this world﴾, that is, you have only enjoyment in this lowly, base worldly life, ﴿then to Us is your return﴾, that is, your destination and your final place, ﴿and We will inform you﴾, that is, We will tell you of all your deeds and repay you for them in full. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame none but himself.

God, blessed and exalted, has set forth a parable of the life of this world, its adornment, and how swiftly it passes away and vanishes, using the plant that God brings forth from the earth by means of the water He sends down from the sky: that which people eat, such as grain and fruit, in their many kinds and varieties, and what livestock eat, such as fodder and clover and other things. ﴿Until, when the earth takes on its adornment and becomes beautified﴾, that is, its fleeting finery, ﴿and its people think they have power over it﴾, meaning those who sowed and planted it, ﴿they think they are able to harvest it﴾, that is, to cut and gather it. ﴿While they are in that state, there comes upon it a thunderbolt or a sudden wind, which dries up its leaves and destroys its fruit.﴾ For this reason He said: ﴿Our command came upon it by night or by day, and We made it a harvested field, as though it had not flourished yesterday﴾, that is, dry stubble after its greenness and freshness, ﴿as though it had never been lush before﴾, meaning as though it had never been beautiful before that.

Qatadah said: ﴿as though it had not flourished﴾ means as though it had not enjoyed prosperity.

Likewise, worldly affairs, once they have gone, are as though they had never been. For this reason it has come in the hadith (the authentic one): "A man from among the most prosperous people of the world will be brought forth and dipped once into the Fire, and then it will be said to him, 'Have you ever seen any good? Has any blessing ever passed you by?' He will say, 'No.' And a man from among the most wretched people of the world will be brought forth and dipped once into bliss, and then it will be said to him, 'Have you ever seen any hardship? Has any misery ever befallen you?' He will say, 'No.'" [Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4321]

God, speaking of those who were destroyed, said: ﴿So they awoke in their homes, lifeless, as though they had never dwelt there﴾ [Hud 11:94–95].

Then God said: ﴿Thus do We detail the signs﴾, that is, We make clear the proofs and evidences, ﴿for a people who reflect﴾, so that they may take heed from this parable of the world's swift departure from its people, even though they are deceived by it and cling to its promises, while it slips away from them. For its nature is to flee from one who seeks it and to be sought by one who flees from it. God has struck the parable of the life of this world with the vegetation of the earth in more than one verse of His Mighty Book. He said in Surat al-Kahf: ﴿And set forth for them the parable of the life of this world: it is like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, and then it becomes dry stalks which the winds scatter. And God is ever Able over all things﴾ [al-Kahf 18:45]. Similarly, in Surat az-Zumar [39:21] and Surat al-Hadid [57:20], He strikes the parable of the life of this world as water.

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith narrated to me, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, who said: I heard Marwan (meaning Ibn al-Hakam) reciting from the pulpit: "And it was beautified, and its people thought they had power over it, and God would not destroy it except for the sins of its people." He said: I have read it, but it is not in the Mushaf (the codex). ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas said: "This is how Ibn ʿAbbas recites it." So they sent to Ibn ʿAbbas, and he said: "This is how Ubayy ibn Kaʿb taught me." [Tafsir al-Tabari 15/57. Shaykh Mahmud Shakir noted in his footnote that this chain is lost (hâlik).]

This is an unusual reading, and it seems to be an addition to the tafsir.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And God calls to the Abode of Peace﴾ up to the end of the verse. When God had mentioned the world and how swiftly it passes and perishes, He encouraged people toward Paradise and called them to it, and He named it the Abode of Peace, meaning free from calamities, deficiencies, and misfortunes. He said: ﴿And God calls to the Abode of Peace, and guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾

Ayyub narrated from Abu Qilabah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "It was said to me: Let your eye sleep, let your heart understand, and let your ear listen. So my eye slept, my heart understood, and my ear listened. Then it was said: A lord built a house, then prepared a feast and sent a summoner. Whoever answers the summoner enters the house, eats from the feast, and the lord is pleased with him. Whoever does not answer the summoner does not enter the house, does not eat from the feast, and the lord is not pleased with him. So God is the Lord, the house is Islam, the feast is Paradise, and the summoner is Muhammad ﷺ." [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, 15/60.]

This is a mursal hadith (one in which the chain omits the Companion who heard it from the Prophet ﷺ). It has also come with a connected chain, from the narration of al-Layth, from Khalid ibn Yazid [in some copies: Suwayd], from Saʿid ibn Abi Hilal, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ came out to us one day and said: "I saw in a dream as though Jibril was at my head and Mikail at my feet, and one of them said to the other: Set forth a parable for him. He said: Listen, may your ear hear; understand, may your heart understand. Your parable and the parable of your community is like a king who acquired a dwelling, then built a house within it, then prepared a feast in it, then sent a messenger to call the people to his food. Some of them answered the messenger, and some of them abandoned him. So God is the King, the dwelling is Islam, the house is Paradise, and you, O Muhammad, are the messenger. Whoever answers you enters Islam, whoever enters Islam enters Paradise, and whoever enters Paradise eats from it." Narrated by Ibn Jarir. [Tafsir al-Tabari 15/61. al-Bukhari mentioned it in his Sahih with no. 7281 as a mu'allaq (suspended) report. al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan with no. 2860 through Qutaybah from al-Layth, and said: "This is a mursal hadith; Saʿid ibn Abi Hilal did not meet Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah." He also said: "This hadith has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ through other routes with a more authentic chain than this one." I say: al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih with no. 7281 through Yazid from Sulaym ibn Hayyan, from Saʿid ibn Abi Maryam, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, in similar wording.]

What is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and distracting." He said: And this was revealed in the Qur'an in His words: ﴿And God calls to the Abode of Peace, and guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. [Tafsir al-Tabari 15/60. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (5/197) through Hammam from Qatadah, in similar wording.]

[Tafsir al-Tabari 15/61. al-Bukhari mentioned it in his Sahih with no. 7281 as a mu'allaq (suspended) report. al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Sunan with no. 2860 through Qutaybah from al-Layth, and said: "This is a mursal hadith; Saʿid ibn Abi Hilal did not meet Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah." He also said: "This hadith has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ through other routes with a more authentic chain than this one." I say: al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih with no. 7281 through Yazid from Sulaym ibn Hayyan, from Saʿid ibn Abi Maryam, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, in similar wording.]

Qatadah said: Khulayd al-ʿAsri narrated to me, from Abu al-Darda, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no day on which the sun rises except that two angels stand on either side of it, calling out so that all of God's creation hears them, except the two weighty ones (humans and jinn): O people, come to your Lord! What is little and sufficient is better than what is abundant and distracting." He said: And this was revealed in the Qur'an in His words: ﴿And God calls to the Abode of Peace, and guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. [Tafsir al-Tabari 15/60. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (5/197) through Hammam from Qatadah, in similar wording.]

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 10, verse 26:

God, exalted is He, informs us that for those who do good in this world, through faith and righteous deeds, He will give in exchange the best reward (al-husna) in the Hereafter, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman: 60].

* *

As for His words ﴿and an increase﴾, it refers to the multiplication of the reward for good deeds, from ten times its like up to seven hundred times, and beyond that. It also includes what God gives them in the Gardens of palaces, the maidens (houris), and His good pleasure with them, and what He has hidden for them of the delight of the eyes. The best and highest of this is gazing upon His Noble Face, for this is an increase greater than everything else they have been given. They do not deserve it by their deeds; rather, it is by His grace and mercy. The interpretation of the increase as gazing upon the Noble Face of God has been related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, [al-Baghawi said: Abu Musa, and 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit,] Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, Mujahid, Ikrimah, 'Amir ibn Sa'd, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and others among the early and later scholars.

Many hadiths have been transmitted about this from the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Among them is what Imam Ahmad narrated:

 'Affan told us: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿For those who have done good is the best reward and more﴾, and he said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hellfire enter the Fire, a caller will call out: 'O people of Paradise, you have a promise from God which He wishes to fulfill for you.' They will say: 'And what is it? Has He not made our scales heavy, whitened our faces, admitted us into Paradise, and saved us from the Fire?' He said: 'Then the veil will be lifted from them, and they will look upon Him. By God, God has given them nothing more beloved to them than gazing upon Him, and nothing more delightful to their eyes.'"

Muslim and a group of the imams narrated it in the same way, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah. [Sahih Muslim, no. 181. It is also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. 2552; al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11234; and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. 187.] Ibn Jarir said: Yunus informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Shabib informed us, from Aban, [from Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi], that he heard Abu Musa al-Ash'ari narrate from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "On the Day of Resurrection, God will send a caller who will call out, 'O people of Paradise!' with a voice heard by the first and the last of them: 'Indeed God has promised you the best reward (al-husna) and more. The best reward is Paradise, and the more is gazing upon the Face of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic.'"

[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/65). Ibn Wahb narrated from Shabib weak (munkar) reports, and Aban ibn Abi 'Ayyash is weak.] It was also narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Abu Tamimah al-Hujaymi, with the same wording.

Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn Humayd told us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding His words ﴿For those who have done good is the best reward and more﴾, that he said: "Gazing upon the Face of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic." [Tafsir al-Tabari (15/68). Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (5/204) through Muhammad ibn Humayd with the same wording, and said: "Strange from the hadith of 'Ata' and Ibn Jurayj; it is related only by Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar." Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar is weak.]

He also said: 'Abd al-Rahim told us, 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, I heard Zuhayr from one who heard Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b told us that he asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿For those who have done good is the best reward and more﴾. He said: "The best reward is Paradise, and the more is gazing upon the Face of God, Mighty and Majestic." [Tafsir al-Tabari (15/69). Al-Lalika'i narrated it in al-Sunnah, no. 780, through several chains from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, from one who heard Abu al-'Aliyah narrate from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ).]

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it from the hadith of Zuhayr, with the same wording.

* *

As for God's words ﴿And no dust nor humiliation shall cover their faces﴾: "dust" (qatar) means darkness and blackness on the plains of the Gathering, just as the dust and dullness (ghubrah) cover the faces of the disbelievers and the wicked. ﴿Nor humiliation﴾ means disgrace and lowliness; that is, no humiliation befalls them inwardly or outwardly. Rather, as God, exalted is He, said concerning them: ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day and gave them radiance and joy﴾, meaning radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts. May God make us of them, by His grace and mercy. Amen.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 10, verse 27:

When Allah, the Exalted, informed us about the state of the happy people, for whom good deeds are multiplied and who are granted increase beyond that, He turned to mention the state of the wretched. He mentioned His justice concerning them, and that He recompenses them for an evil deed with its like, adding nothing to it beyond that. ﴿And humiliation will cover them﴾, meaning: a humiliation will overtake and overwhelm them because of their sins and their fear of them, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And you will see them presented before it, humbled by humiliation, looking with a furtive glance﴾ [Ash-Shura: 45]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only defers them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly, [They will be] hastening, with heads raised, their glance not returning to them, and their hearts empty.* And warn mankind of the Day the punishment comes to them﴾ [Ibrahim: 42-44]. And His saying ﴿They will have no protector from Allah﴾, meaning: no preventer and no shield to protect them from the punishment, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿On that Day man will say, "Where is the escape?" No! There is no refuge. To your Lord, that Day, is the place of rest﴾ [Al-Qiyamah: 10-12].

* *

His saying: ﴿As if their faces were covered with pieces of the night, in darkness﴾ is an informing about the blackness of their faces in the Hereafter, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black. As for those whose faces turned black, [it will be said], "Did you disbelieve after your belief? So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve." And as for those whose faces turned white, they will be in the mercy of Allah, wherein they will abide eternally﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 106-107], and as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, joyful; and faces that Day will be dust-covered, overtaken by darkness. Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾ [Abasa: 38-42]. And the verse.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the Day We gather them﴾, that is, all the people of the earth, of jinn and mankind, the righteous and the wicked, as He said: ﴿And We gathered them together, and left out none of them﴾ [al-Kahf: 47].

﴿Then We will say to those who associated others with Allah: "Stay in your place, you and your partners"﴾, that is, remain, you and those you worshipped, in a specific place where you are separated from the station of the believers, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And separate yourselves today, O criminals﴾ [Ya-Sin: 59]. He also said: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, that Day they will be divided﴾ [ar-Rum: 14], and in another verse: ﴿That Day they will be split apart﴾ [ar-Rum: 43], meaning they will become two groups. This happens when the Lord, the Exalted, comes to judge between the creatures. For this reason it was said: [on that Day] the believers will seek intercession from Allah, the Exalted, that He come to judge between them and relieve us from this place where we stand. The hadith of intercession is related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (no. 4476) from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him. In another hadith: "We will be on the Day of Resurrection upon a mound above the people." [Note: in A: "the Fire".] It is related by Ahmad in al-Musnad (3/345) from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Kawm means an elevated, high place.

Allah the Exalted said in this noble verse, reporting what He will command the polytheists and their idols on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Stay in your place, you and your partners. Then We will separate them. And their partners will say: "You did not used to worship us"﴾. They denied their worship and disowned them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿No! They will deny their worship of them and will be opposed to them﴾ [Maryam: 82], and He said: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾ [al-Baqarah: 166], and He said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their supplication? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 5-6].

In this verse, reporting the words of the partners, in their reply to those who worshipped them when they claimed that worship: ﴿Sufficient is Allah as a witness between us and you; indeed we were unaware of your worship﴾, that is, we did not perceive it or know of it; rather, you used to worship us without our knowing about you, and Allah is a witness between us and you that we did not call you to worship us, nor did we command you to it, nor were we pleased with you for that.

In this there is a great rebuke to the polytheists who worshipped other than Allah alongside Him, those who neither hear nor see and cannot benefit them at all, and who did not command them to that, nor were pleased with it, nor willed it. Rather, they disown them at a time when they are most in need of them, while they have abandoned the worship of the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, the All-Powerful over everything, the All-Knowing of everything, who sent His messengers and revealed His books, commanding that He alone be worshipped without partner and forbidding the worship of anything besides Him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"; then among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was decreed﴾ [an-Nahl: 36]. Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya: 25], and He said: ﴿And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint deities other than the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 45].

The polytheists are of many kinds and categories. Allah has mentioned them in His Book, explained their conditions and their statements, and refuted them in the most complete refutation for what they were upon.

* *

His saying: ﴿There every soul will be [put to the test for] what it sent before﴾, that is, in the place of reckoning on the Day of Resurrection every soul will be tested and will know what it sent before of [its deeds of] good and evil, as Allah said: ﴿The Day when secrets will be examined﴾ [at-Tariq: 9], and Allah said: ﴿On that Day man will be informed of what he sent ahead and kept back﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13], and Allah said: ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will encounter spread open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner"﴾ [al-Isra: 13-14].

Some have read it as ﴿tatlu﴾ [every soul will recite what it sent before], and some explained it as recitation; some explained it as meaning it will follow what it sent before of good and evil; and some explained it with the hadith: "Every nation will follow what it used to worship: whoever used to worship the sun will follow the sun, whoever used to worship the moon will follow the moon, and whoever used to worship the taghut will follow the taghut..." until the end of the hadith. It is related by Muslim in his Sahih (no. 182) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And they will be returned to Allah, their true Master﴾, that is, all matters will return to Allah, the Just Judge, who will distinguish them, admitting the people of Paradise to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire.

﴿And lost from them﴾, that is, gone away from the polytheists, ﴿is what they used to invent﴾, that is, what they used to worship besides Allah as a fabrication against Him.

The Exalted argues against the polytheists using their own acknowledgement of His oneness and lordship, as proof of the oneness of the Divine. He says: ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?"﴾ That is, who is it that sends down rain from the sky, so that by His power and will He splits the earth open, and brings forth from it ﴿grain, grapes, herbage, olives, palm trees, enclosed gardens of dense trees, fruits and pasture﴾ [Abasa 80:27–31]? Is there a god alongside God? They will say, "God." ﴿Or who is it that provides for you if He withholds His provision?﴾ [al-Mulk 67:21]. Likewise His saying: ﴿Or who controls hearing and sight?﴾ [Yunus 10:31]. That is, who has given you this hearing faculty and this sight faculty? If He willed, He could take them away and strip you of them, as He said: ﴿Say, "It is He who produced you and made for you hearing, sight and hearts; little are you grateful"﴾ [al-Mulk 67:23]. And He said: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if God took away your hearing and your sight and sealed over your hearts, what god other than God could bring them back to you?"﴾ [al-An'am 6:46].

* *

His saying: ﴿And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living?﴾ That is, by His great power and His all-encompassing favour. The disagreement concerning this has already been mentioned, and that the verse is general in all of that.

* *

His saying: ﴿And who disposes of the affair?﴾ That is, in whose hand is the dominion of everything? He grants protection and no one can be given protection against Him. He is the Disposer, the Judge, whose judgment has no repeller, and He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him; every day He is engaged in some affair﴾ [al-Rahman 55:29]. So the whole dominion, the upper and the lower, and whatever is in them of angels, humans and jinn, are all needy of Him, servants of Him, subservient to Him. ﴿They will say, "God."﴾ That is, they know this and acknowledge it. ﴿So say: "Will you not then be wary [of Him]?"﴾ That is, will you not fear Him, lest you worship alongside Him something other than Him, by your own opinions and your ignorance?

* *

His saying: ﴿That is God, your true Lord. So what is there after the truth but error? * *

Say: "God guides to the truth."﴾ That is: you know that your partners are not able to guide anyone who has gone astray; rather, it is God who guides the bewildered and the misguided and turns hearts from error to rectitude, the One besides whom there is no god.

* *

His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring a surah like it and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."﴾ Meaning: if you claim and fabricate and doubt that this is from Allah, and say falsely and baselessly, "This is from Muhammad," then Muhammad is a human like you, and he came, as you claim, with this Qur'an. Meaning: a report about what has passed and what will come, and a judgment among people by the Shari'ah which Allah loves and is pleased with.

* *

His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring a surah like it and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."﴾ Meaning: if you claim and fabricate and doubt that this is from Allah, and say falsely and baselessly, "This is from Muhammad," then Muhammad is a human like you, and he came, as you claim, with this Qur'an. So bring yourselves a surah like it, meaning of the same kind as the Qur'an, and seek help in that from everyone you are able to, of mankind and jinn.

This is the third stage of the challenge. He, the Exalted, challenged them and called upon them, if they were truthful in their claim that it is from Muhammad, to oppose it with something like what he brought, by himself, and seek help from whomever they wish. He informed them that they would not be able to do that, and that they had no way to it. So He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to each other assistants."﴾ [al-Isra': 88]. Then He lowered the challenge for them to ten surahs of it, saying at the beginning of Surah Hud: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."﴾ [Hud: 13]. Then He lowered it further to a single surah, saying in this surah: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring a surah like it and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."﴾. Likewise in Surah al-Baqarah, which is Madani, He challenged them with a surah from it, and informed them that they would never be able to do that, saying: ﴿But if you do not, and you will never do, then fear the Fire﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 24].

Eloquence was among their natural dispositions, and their poetry and their Mu'allaqat reached the utmost limit in this field. But there came to them from Allah what no one could withstand. For this reason, whoever among them believed did so because he recognized the eloquence of this speech, its sweetness, its firmness, its beauty, its benefit, and its excellence. They were the most knowledgeable of people about it, the most understanding of it, the most following of it, and the most submissive to it. Just as the magicians recognized, because of their knowledge of the arts of magic, that what Musa, peace be upon him, did could only proceed from one supported, guided, and sent by Allah, and that this could not be achieved by a human except by the permission of Allah. Likewise 'Isa, peace be upon him, was sent in an age of physicians and those who treat the sick, and he healed the blind and the leper and brought the dead to life by the permission of Allah, and such a thing has no place for medicine or cure in it. So whoever among them recognized it knew that he was the servant of Allah and His messenger. For this reason it is reported in the Sahih, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "There is no prophet among the prophets except that he was given signs such that mankind believed in their like, but what I was given is a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope that I will have the most followers among them."¹

¹ Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (4981), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (152), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.

* *

His saying: ﴿Rather, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge, and its interpretation has not yet come to them.﴾ He says: rather, these people denied the Qur'an, and they did not understand it nor recognize it. ﴿And its interpretation has not yet come to them﴾, meaning: they had not gained what is in it of guidance and the religion of truth until the time of their denial of it, out of ignorance and foolishness. ﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾, meaning: of the earlier nations. ﴿So see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: see how We destroyed them for their denial of Our messengers, through wrongdoing, arrogance, disbelief, obstinacy, and ignorance. So beware, O deniers, lest there befall you what befell them.

* *

His saying: ﴿And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters.﴾ Meaning: and among those to whom you, O Muhammad, were sent, there are those who will believe in this Qur'an, follow you, and benefit from what you were sent with. ﴿And among them are those who do not believe in it﴾, rather they will die upon that and be resurrected upon it. ﴿And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters﴾, meaning: He is most knowing of who deserves guidance and so guides him, and who deserves misguidance and so misguides him. He is the Just who does not oppress, but gives each what he deserves. Blessed and exalted is He, sanctified and far removed from imperfection; there is no god but Him.

This is a statement of the inimitability of the Qur'an (i'jaz al-Qur'an), and that mankind cannot produce its like, nor ten surahs, nor a single surah like it. This is because of its eloquence (fasahah), its rhetorical power (balaghah), its conciseness (wajazah), its sweetness (halawah), and its inclusion of noble meanings beneficial in this world and the Hereafter. It can only come from Allah, who is not like anything in His essence, His attributes, His actions, or His speech. His speech is not like the speech of creatures. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And this Qur'an could not have been produced by other than Allah﴾, meaning: the like of this Qur'an can only come from Allah, and this is not similar to human speech. ﴿But it is a confirmation of that which was before it﴾, meaning of the earlier scriptures, ﴿and a detailed explanation of the Book﴾, and it is a witness over them and an explanation of what occurred in them of distortion (tahrif), misinterpretation (ta'wil), and alteration (tabdil).

Allah says to His Prophet ﷺ: "And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], these polytheists, then disassociate yourself from them and from their deeds. ﴿Say: 'To me is my deed, and to you is your deed.'﴾" This is like His saying: ﴿Say, "O disbelievers! I do not worship what you worship. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped. Nor are you worshippers of what I worship. To you is your religion, and to me is my religion."﴾ [Al-Kafirun]. And Ibrahim al-Khalil (the Friend of Allah) and his followers said to their polytheist people: ﴿Indeed, we are free from you and from what you worship besides Allah. We have disbelieved in you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone﴾ [Al-Mumtahanah: 4].

* *

His saying: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾, meaning: they hear your good speech, the Great Qur'an, and the sound, eloquent Hadiths, which are beneficial for hearts, bodies and religions. In this there is great sufficiency. But that is not up to you or to them, for you cannot make the deaf hear, and he is the one who is hard of hearing. Likewise, you cannot guide these people, except if Allah wills.

﴿And among them are those who look at you﴾, meaning: they look at you and at what Allah has given you of gravity, good bearing, great character, and clear evidence of your prophethood, for people of insight and understanding. Yet these people look just as others do, and they gain none of the guidance that others gain. Rather, the believers look at you with the eye of reverence, and the disbelievers look at you with the eye of contempt. ﴿And when they see you, they take you in mockery only: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger? He had almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast to them." And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in the way﴾ [Al-Furqan: 41, 42].

Then Allah informs that He does not wrong anyone at all, even though He guided by it whom He guided [from error], and gave sight by it to the blind, opened by it eyes that were blind, ears that were deaf, and hearts that were veiled, and led astray from faith by it others. He is the Judge who disposes of His dominion as He wills, who is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned, by virtue of His knowledge, wisdom and justice. Therefore Allah said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, but people wrong themselves﴾.

And in the Hadith narrated from Abu Dharr, from the Prophet ﷺ, related from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself, and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another." ...up to his saying at its end: "O My servants, they are only your deeds which I count for you, then I repay you for them. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame no one but himself." Narrated by Muslim in full. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2577]
