Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him: Allah the Exalted says, reminding mankind of the Hour and of their being gathered from their graves to the plains of the Resurrection: "As if they had not remained [in the world] but an hour of a day" on the day they arrive at it. As He said: ﴿As if they had not remained but an evening or a morning of it﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]. He also said: ﴿On the Day the Horn is blown, We will gather the criminals that Day, blue-eyed. They will whisper among themselves, "You remained not but ten [days]." We know best what they will say when their most intelligent in way says, "You remained not but a day."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102-104]. And He said: ﴿And on the Day the Hour appears, the criminals will swear that they remained not but an hour. Thus were they deluded.﴾ ﴿But those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You remained, by the decree of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection, but you were not aware."﴾ [ar-Rum: 55-56].

All of this is evidence of how short the life of this world will seem in the Hereafter, as He said: ﴿He will say, "How long did you remain on earth in number of years?" They will say, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who keep count." He will say, "You remained not but a little, if only you had known."﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 112-114].

* *

His saying: ﴿They will recognize one another among themselves﴾ means that sons will recognize their fathers and relatives will recognize one another, as they did in the world; but each one will be preoccupied with himself. ﴿So when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101]. He also said: ﴿And no intimate friend will ask after an intimate friend, though they will be made to see them. The criminal would wish to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day by his children, his wife, his brother, his close family who shelters him, and everyone on earth, then that it might save him. No!﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 10-15].

* *

His saying: ﴿They have certainly lost who denied the meeting with Allah, and they were not guided﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾ [al-Mursalat: 15]. Because they lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss. This is the great loss, and there is no loss greater than the loss of one who is separated from his loved ones on the Day of regret and remorse.

Allah the Exalted says, addressing His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them﴾, that is, We take vengeance upon them during your lifetime so that your eye may be comforted by them, ﴿or We cause you to die, then to Us is their return﴾, that is, their final destination and place of turning. And Allah is Witness over their deeds after you.

Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, 'Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, Dawud ibn al-Jarud narrated to us, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "My community was presented to me last night at this chamber, its first and its last. A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you were shown those who have been created; so how about those who have not yet been created?' He said: 'Form them for me in clay, until I recognise a person among them better than one of you recognises his companion.'" [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/181)]

It was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from 'Uqbah ibn Mukram, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid, with similar wording. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/181). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/69): "In it is Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, who is a liar."]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And for every community there is a messenger. When their messenger comes﴾, Mujahid said: this means the Day of Resurrection.

﴿It will be judged between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾. As He said: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them with truth, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Az-Zumar: 69]. So every community is presented to Allah in the presence of its messenger, and the book of its deeds, containing good and evil, is placed as a witness against them, and their guardian angels are also witnesses, community after community. This noble community, although it is the last of the communities in creation, is the first of the communities on the Day of Resurrection to be judged between and to be given judgment, as has come in the two Sahihs from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, the ones for whom judgment is given before the creatures." [This wording is in Sahih Muslim, no. 856, from the hadith of Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him); al-Bukhari narrated its beginning, no. 876, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).] Thus its community has won the prize of precedence because of the nobility of its Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, always, until the Day of Judgment.

Allah the Exalted says, addressing His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them﴾, that is, We take vengeance upon them during your lifetime so that your eye may be comforted by them, ﴿or We cause you to die, then to Us is their return﴾, that is, their final destination and place of turning. And Allah is Witness over their deeds after you.

Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, 'Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi narrated to us, Dawud ibn al-Jarud narrated to us, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "My community was presented to me last night at this chamber, its first and its last. A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you were shown those who have been created; so how about those who have not yet been created?' He said: 'Form them for me in clay, until I recognise a person among them better than one of you recognises his companion.'" [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/181)]

It was also narrated by Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah, from 'Uqbah ibn Mukram, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Abu al-Tufayl, from Hudhayfah ibn Asid, with similar wording. [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/181). Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10/69): "In it is Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, who is a liar."]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And for every community there is a messenger. When their messenger comes﴾, Mujahid said: this means the Day of Resurrection.

﴿It will be judged between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾. As He said: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them with truth, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Az-Zumar: 69]. So every community is presented to Allah in the presence of its messenger, and the book of its deeds, containing good and evil, is placed as a witness against them, and their guardian angels are also witnesses, community after community. This noble community, although it is the last of the communities in creation, is the first of the communities on the Day of Resurrection to be judged between and to be given judgment, as has come in the two Sahihs from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, the ones for whom judgment is given before the creatures." [This wording is in Sahih Muslim, no. 856, from the hadith of Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him); al-Bukhari narrated its beginning, no. 876, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).] Thus its community has won the prize of precedence because of the nobility of its Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, always, until the Day of Judgment.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 10 (Yunus), verses 48–52:

He, exalted is He, says, informing about the disbelief of these polytheists in their hastening of the punishment and their asking about its time before it is determined, which has no benefit for them, as He said: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [ash-Shura: 18], meaning: it will certainly occur and come to pass, even if they do not know its exact time. For this reason He guided His Messenger ﷺ to answer them, saying: ﴿Say: I possess no power to benefit or harm myself except as Allah wills﴾, meaning: I do not say except what He has taught me, and I have no power over anything of what He has kept to Himself except that He informs me of it. I am His servant and His Messenger to you, and I have informed you of the coming of the Hour and that it will certainly occur, but He has not informed me of its time. ﴿But for every nation there is a term﴾, meaning: for every generation there is a period of life that has been decreed. So when their term has ended, ﴿they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it﴾, as He said: ﴿And Allah will never delay a soul when its term has come﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 11]. Then He informed them that the punishment of Allah will come upon them suddenly, saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if His punishment came upon you by night or by day﴾, meaning: at night or during the day, ﴿what part of it would the criminals be hastening? Then, when it has occurred, will you believe in it?﴾ This means that when the punishment comes upon them they will say: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteousness; indeed, we are certain﴾ [as-Sajdah: 12]. And He said: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith was not going to benefit them when they saw Our might. [This is] the established way of Allah which has preceded among His servants. And the disbelievers were lost therein﴾ [Ghafir: 84–85].

﴿Then it will be said to those who wronged: Taste the punishment of eternity﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection it will be said to them this, as a rebuke and reproach, like His saying: ﴿On the Day they will be pushed into the fire of Hell with a violent push. "This is the Fire which you used to deny. Is this magic, or is it that you do not see? Burn therein; so bear it patiently or do not bear it patiently; it is all the same for you. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do."﴾ [at-Tur: 13–16].

Allah says: "They ask you, 'Is it true?'" That is, is the Resurrection (al-Ma'ad) true, the raising from the graves after the bodies have turned to dust? "Say: 'Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true, and you cannot escape (Allah).'" That is, your turning to dust is no obstacle that could prevent Allah from restoring you, just as He originated you from non-existence: "Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is." [Ya-Sin: 82]

This verse has no parallel in the Qur'an except two others. Allah commands His Messenger to swear by Him against those who denied the Return (al-Ma'ad), in Surah Saba': "And those who disbelieve say, 'The Hour will not come to us.' Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.'" [Saba': 3] And in at-Taghabun: "Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will be informed of what you did. And that is easy for Allah.'" [at-Taghabun: 7]

Then Allah informs that when the Resurrection occurs, the disbeliever will wish that he could ransom himself from the punishment of Allah with the filling of the earth in gold. "And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, and it will be judged between them with justice," that is, with truth, "and they will not be wronged."

Allah says: "They ask you, 'Is it true?'" That is, is the Resurrection (al-Ma'ad) true, the raising from the graves after the bodies have turned to dust? "Say: 'Yes, by my Lord, it is indeed true, and you cannot escape (Allah).'" [Ya-Sin: 82]

Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected; then you will be informed of what you did. And that is easy for Allah.'" [at-Taghabun: 7]

"And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, and it will be judged between them with justice," that is, with truth, "and they will not be wronged."

It tells us, exalted is He, that He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth, that His promise is true and will certainly come to pass, that He gives life and causes death, and to Him they will return, and that He is capable of all of that, knowing of what has scattered of bodies and been torn apart throughout all regions of the earth, the seas and the deserts [Glorified is He and exalted is He; hallowed are His names and mighty is His praise]. [[Addition from manuscript A.]]

It tells us, exalted is He, that He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth, that His promise is true and will certainly come to pass, that He gives life and causes death, and to Him they will return, and that He is capable of all of that, knowing of what has scattered of bodies and been torn apart throughout all regions of the earth, the seas and the deserts [Glorified is He and exalted is He; hallowed are His names and mighty is His praise]. [[Addition from manuscript A.]]

He, the Exalted, says, enumerating the favours He bestowed on His creation through the Mighty Qur'an that He sent down to His noble Messenger:

﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord﴾, meaning: a restraint from indecencies. ﴿And a healing for what is in the breasts﴾, meaning: from doubts and suspicions, and this is the removal of what is in them of filth and defilement. ﴿And guidance and mercy﴾, meaning: guidance and mercy from Allah, the Exalted, are obtained by them. This applies only to those who believe in it, who affirm it and are certain of what it contains, as He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾ [al-Isra' 17:82]. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Say, it is for those who believe a guidance and a healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them. Those are being called from a distant place﴾ [Fussilat 41:44].

* *

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say, in the bounty of Allah and His mercy, so in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾ [Yunus 10:58], meaning: in this which has come to them from Allah, the guidance and the religion of truth, let them rejoice, for it is the most fitting thing for them to rejoice in. ﴿It is better than what they accumulate﴾, meaning: than the trash of this world and what is in it of the fleeting splendour that will certainly pass away.

Ibn Abi Hatim said in explaining this verse: "It was mentioned from Baqiyyah, meaning Ibn al-Walid, from Safwan ibn Amr, who said: I heard Ayfa' ibn Abd al-Kula'i say: When the kharaj (land tax) of Iraq was brought to Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, Umar went out with a freedman of his, and Umar began counting the camels, and they were more than that. Umar began to say: All praise is due to Allah, the Exalted. And his freedman said: By Allah, this is from the bounty of Allah and His mercy. So Umar said: You have lied. This is not it; it is what Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Say, in the bounty of Allah and His mercy, so in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾. And this is part of what they accumulate."

This was also traced back in its chain by the Hafiz (hadith master) Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani, who narrated it from Abu Zur'ah al-Dimashqi, from Haywah ibn Shurayh, from Baqiyyah, and mentioned it. [Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (4/368), attributing it to Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani.]

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: it was revealed as a rebuke to the polytheists for what they used to forbid and permit of the baha'ir (she-camels whose ears were slit), the sawa'ib (animals released for their gods), and the wasaya (ordinances), like His saying, ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has created of the crops and livestock﴾ [al-An'am: 136], and the verses that follow.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Abu al-Ahwas, who is Awf ibn [Malik ibn] [[Addition from T, A, and al-Musnad.]] Nadhlah, narrating from his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while my appearance was unkempt, and he said: "Do you have any wealth?" I said: "Yes." He said: "What kind of wealth?" I said: "Of every kind of wealth: camels, slaves, horses and sheep." He said: "When Allah gives you wealth, let the effect of it be seen upon you." And he said: "Do the camels of your people give birth to whole-eared ones, so that you go to one of them and slit its ears and say, 'This is a bahira,' and tear its skin and say, 'This is a sarum,' and forbid it to yourself and your family?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what Allah has given you is lawful for you. The strength of Allah is greater than your strength, and the sharpness of Allah's blade is greater than your blade," and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. [[al-Musnad (3/473).]]

Then he narrated it from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Abu al-Za'ra' Amr ibn Amr, from his paternal uncle Abu al-Ahwas. [[al-Musnad (4/137).]] And from Bahz ibn Asad, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abu al-Ahwas, with the same. [[al-Musnad (3/473).]] This is a good hadith with a strong chain of narration.

God rebuked those who forbid what God has made lawful, or make lawful what He has forbidden, merely by opinions and desires that have no basis and no proof. Then He threatened them for that on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿And what will be the thought of those who fabricate lies against God on the Day of Resurrection?﴾, that is, what do they think will be done to them on the day of their return to Us, the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, Ibn Jarir said: in His not hastening to punish them in this world.

I say: It is also possible that the meaning is: He is full of bounty toward mankind in what He has permitted them of the benefits He created in this world, and He has forbidden to them only what is harmful to them in their worldly life or their religion.

﴿But most of them do not give thanks﴾, rather they forbid what Allah has bestowed upon them, and restrict themselves, making some things lawful and some things unlawful. The polytheists fell into this regarding what they legislated for themselves, and the People of the Book regarding what they innovated in their religion. Ibn Abi Hatim said in his tafsir of this verse: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari narrated to us, Rabah narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Musa ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people of Allah's friendship (wilayah) will be brought, and they will stand before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in three categories. He said: A man from the first category will be brought, and He will say: "My servant, why did you act?" He will say: "My Lord, You created Paradise and its trees, its fruits and its rivers, its maidens and its bliss, and what You prepared in it for the people of Your obedience. So I kept my night awake and my day thirsty, longing for it." He said: Allah, Most High, will say: "My servant, you acted only for Paradise. This is Paradise, so enter it. And of My bounty upon you, I have freed you from the Fire," [And of My bounty upon you is that I admit you into My Paradise.] He said: So he and those with him enter Paradise.

He said: Then a man from the second category will be brought, and He will say: "My servant, why did you act?" He will say: "My Lord, You created a Fire, its shackles, its blaze, its scorching winds and its boiling water, and what You prepared in it for Your enemies and the people of Your disobedience. So I kept my night awake and my day thirsty, out of fear of it." He will say: "My servant, you acted only out of fear of My Fire. I have freed you from the Fire, and of My bounty upon you is that I admit you into My Paradise." So he and those with him enter Paradise.

Then a man from the third category will be brought, and He will say: "My servant, why did you act?" He will say: "My Lord, out of love for You and longing for You. By Your might, I kept my night awake and my day thirsty, longing for You and loving You." Blessed and Exalted will say: "My servant, you acted only out of love for Me and longing for Me." Then the Lord, Majestic in His majesty, will manifest Himself to him and say: "Here I am, look at Me." Then He will say: "Of My bounty upon you, I free you from the Fire, I grant you My Paradise, I visit you with My angels, and I greet you Myself." So he and those with him enter Paradise.

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: it was revealed as a rebuke to the polytheists for what they used to forbid and permit of the baha'ir (she-camels whose ears were slit), the sawa'ib (animals released for their gods), and the wasaya (ordinances), like His saying, ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has created of the crops and livestock﴾ [al-An'am: 136], and the verses that follow.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Abu al-Ahwas, who is Awf ibn [Malik ibn] [[Addition from T, A, and al-Musnad.]] Nadhlah, narrating from his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while my appearance was unkempt, and he said: "Do you have any wealth?" I said: "Yes." He said: "What kind of wealth?" I said: "Of every kind of wealth: camels, slaves, horses and sheep." He said: "When Allah gives you wealth, let the effect of it be seen upon you." And he said: "Do the camels of your people give birth to whole-eared ones, so that you go to one of them and slit its ears and say, 'This is a bahira,' and tear its skin and say, 'This is a sarum,' and forbid it to yourself and your family?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what Allah has given you is lawful for you. The strength of Allah is greater than your strength, and the sharpness of Allah's blade is greater than your blade," and he mentioned the rest of the hadith. [[al-Musnad (3/473).]]

Then he narrated it from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Abu al-Za'ra' Amr ibn Amr, from his paternal uncle Abu al-Ahwas. [[al-Musnad (4/137).]] And from Bahz ibn Asad, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abu al-Ahwas, with the same. [[al-Musnad (3/473).]] This is a good hadith with a strong chain of narration.

God rebuked those who forbid what God has made lawful, or make lawful what He has forbidden, merely by opinions and desires that have no basis and no proof. Then He threatened them for that on the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿And what will be the thought of those who fabricate lies against God on the Day of Resurrection?﴾, that is, what do they think will be done to them on the day of their return to Us, the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, Ibn Jarir said: in His not hastening to punish them in this world.

I say: It is also possible that the meaning is: He is full of bounty toward mankind in what He has permitted them of the benefits He created in this world, and He has forbidden to them only what is harmful to them in their worldly life or their religion.

﴿But most of them do not give thanks﴾, rather they forbid what Allah has bestowed upon them, and restrict themselves, making some things lawful and some things unlawful. The polytheists fell into this regarding what they legislated for themselves, and the People of the Book regarding what they innovated in their religion. Ibn Abi Hatim said in his tafsir of this verse: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari narrated to us, Rabah narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Musa ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾, he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the people of Allah's friendship (wilayah) will be brought, and they will stand before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in three categories. He said: A man from the first category will be brought, and He will say: "My servant, why did you act?" He will say: "My Lord, You created Paradise and its trees, its fruits and its rivers, its maidens and its bliss, and what You prepared in it for the people of Your obedience. So I kept my night awake and my day thirsty, longing for it." He said: Allah, Most High, will say: "My servant, you acted only for Paradise. This is Paradise, so enter it. And of My bounty upon you, I have freed you from the Fire," [And of My bounty upon you is that I admit you into My Paradise.] He said: So he and those with him enter Paradise.

He said: Then a man from the second category will be brought, and He will say: "My servant, why did you act?" He will say: "My Lord, You created a Fire, its shackles, its blaze, its scorching winds and its boiling water, and what You prepared in it for Your enemies and the people of Your disobedience. So I kept my night awake and my day thirsty, out of fear of it." He will say: "My servant, you acted only out of fear of My Fire. I have freed you from the Fire, and of My bounty upon you is that I admit you into My Paradise." So he and those with him enter Paradise.

Then a man from the third category will be brought, and He will say: "My servant, why did you act?" He will say: "My Lord, out of love for You and longing for You. By Your might, I kept my night awake and my day thirsty, longing for You and loving You." Blessed and Exalted will say: "My servant, you acted only out of love for Me and longing for Me." Then the Lord, Majestic in His majesty, will manifest Himself to him and say: "Here I am, look at Me." Then He will say: "Of My bounty upon you, I free you from the Fire, I grant you My Paradise, I visit you with My angels, and I greet you Myself." So he and those with him enter Paradise.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on Surah 10, verse 61:

God informs His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, that He knows all his conditions and the conditions of his community, and all creatures, at every hour, moment and instant, and that nothing escapes His knowledge and sight, not even an atom's weight (mithqal dharrah) in its insignificance and smallness, in the heavens or on the earth, nor anything smaller or greater than it, except that it is in a Clear Book (kitab mubin). As He says: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen. None knows them but He. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but that it is in a Clear Book.﴾ [Al-An'am: 59]. Thus He informs us that He knows the movement of trees and other inanimate things, and likewise the grazing animals, in His words: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies with its two wings, but that they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.﴾ [Al-An'am: 38]. And He said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that its provision is upon Allah, and He knows its place of lodging and its place of storage. All is in a Clear Book.﴾ [Hud: 6].

If this is His knowledge of the movements of these things, then how much more is His knowledge of the movements of the accountable servants who are commanded to worship, as He says: ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful, who sees you when you stand [for prayer] and your movement among those who prostrate.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 217-219]. Therefore He said: ﴿And you are not in any affair, nor recite from it any Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, except that We are witnesses over you when you are engaged therein.﴾ That is: when you undertake that matter, We are observing you, seeing you and hearing you. For this reason, when Jibril asked him about ihsan (excellence in worship), he, peace be upon him, said: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you." [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (8), from the lengthy hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab.]

God, Exalted is He, informs that His *awliya'* (friends, allies) are those who believed and were God-fearing (*yattaqun*), as their Lord described them. So everyone who was pious was a friend of God: ﴿no fear shall be upon them﴾ regarding what they will face of the terrors of the Resurrection, ﴿nor shall they grieve﴾ over what they left behind in the world.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, and others among the *salaf* (the early righteous generations) said: the friends of God are those who, when they are seen, God is remembered.

This has been transmitted in a *marfu'* hadith (one traced directly to the Prophet ﷺ), as al-Bazzar said:

Ali ibn Harb al-Razi told us, Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Sabiq told us, Ya'qub ibn Abdullah al-Ash'ari (he is al-Qummi) told us, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man said, "O Messenger of God, who are the friends of God?" He said: "Those who, when they are seen, God is remembered." Then al-Bazzar said: It has also been transmitted from Sa'id as *mursal* (a report whose chain omits a Companion).[[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (3626) (Kashf al-Astar). The *mursal* version was narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/119) through Ash'ath ibn Ishaq, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, as a *mursal* report.]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i told us, Ibn Fudayl told us, my father told us, from Umara ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'a ibn Amr ibn Jarir al-Bajali, from Abu Hurayra, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed among the servants of God are servants whom the prophets and martyrs envy (admire)." It was said: "Who are they, O Messenger of God? Perhaps we would love them." He said: "They are people who love one another for the sake of God, not for wealth or lineage between them. Their faces are light, upon pulpits of light. They do not fear when people fear, and they do not grieve when people grieve." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, the friends of God—no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve.﴾[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/20). Al-Nasa'i narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11236) from Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from his father and Umara ibn al-Qa'qa' together, both from Abu Zur'a, from Abu Hurayra, in similar wording. Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih no. (2508) through Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih, from Ibn Fudayl, from Umara ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'a.]]

Then Abu Dawud also narrated it, from the hadith of Jarir, from Umara ibn al-Qa'qa', from Abu Zur'a ibn Amr ibn Jarir, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, with the same wording.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/121) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3527).]]

This chain is also sound (*jayyid*), except that it is *munqati'* (broken) between Abu Zur'a and Umar ibn al-Khattab. And God knows best.

In the hadith of Imam Ahmad, from Abu al-Nadr, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There will come from the scattered peoples and the remote tribes a group between whom no ties of kinship exist, close to one another, who love one another for God's sake and are sincere to one another for God's sake. On the Day of Resurrection God will set for them pulpits of light and seat them upon them. People will be terrified, but they will not be terrified, and they are the friends of God, ﴿upon whom no fear shall come, nor shall they grieve.﴾" The hadith is lengthy.[[Musnad Ahmad (5/343).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Sufyan informed us, from al-A'mash, from Dhakwan Abi Salih, from a man, from Abu al-Darda', may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, regarding His saying: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾. He said: "It is the good dream that a Muslim sees, or that is seen for him."[[Musnad Ahmad (6/445).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu al-Sa'ib told me, Abu Mu'awiya told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from a man from the people of Egypt, from Abu al-Darda', regarding the verse: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾ He said: A man from the people of Egypt asked Abu al-Darda' about this verse. He said: "You have asked about something that I have not heard anyone ask about since a man asked the Messenger of God about it. He said: 'It is the good dream that a Muslim man sees, or that is seen for him. Its good news in this world is [that], and its good news in the Hereafter is [Paradise].'"[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/128) (the bracketed additions are from the manuscripts and al-Tabari).]]

Then Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan, from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from a man of Egypt, that he asked Abu al-Darda' about this verse, and he mentioned something similar to what preceded.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/128). Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan no. (3106) through Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, similarly.]]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me: al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal told us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, from Asim ibn Bahdala, from Abu Salih, who said: I heard Abu al-Darda', and he was asked about: ﴿Those who believed and were God-fearing—for them is good news,﴾ and he mentioned something similar, the same.[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/136). Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in al-Sunan no. (3106) through Ahmad ibn Abda, from Hammad ibn Zayd.]]

Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Aban told us, Yahya told us, from Abu Salama, from Ubada ibn al-Samit, that he asked the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of God, what do you say about the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾?" He said: "You have asked me about something that none of my nation has asked me about, or [he said] none before you has asked." He said: "It is the good dream; the righteous man sees it, or it is seen for him."

Similarly, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it from Imran al-Qattan, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, with the same chain.[[Musnad Ahmad (5/315). It is in Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (583) from Harb ibn Shaddad, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama, who said: "I was told that Ubada ibn al-Samit..." and mentioned it. This is *munqati'* (broken). Ibn Hajar said: "Its narrators are trustworthy, but it is defective, for Abu Salama did not hear from Ubada."]] It was also narrated by al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who mentioned it. Ali ibn al-Mubarak narrated it from Yahya, from Abu Salama, who said: "We were told about Ubada ibn al-Samit, that he asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about this verse," and he mentioned it.

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Humayd al-Himsi told me, Yahya ibn Sa'id told us, Umar ibn Amr ibn Abd al-Ahmusi told us, from Humayd ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: A man came to Ubada ibn al-Samit and said: "There is a verse in the Book of God that I want to ask you about: the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾?" Ubada said: "No one has asked me about it before you. I asked the Prophet of God about it, and he said the same thing: 'No one has asked me about it before you. It is the good dream, which the believing servant sees in sleep, or that is seen for him.'"[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/129).]]

Then he narrated it from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubayda, from Ayyub ibn Khalid ibn Safwan, from Ubada ibn al-Samit, that he said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.﴾ "We have known the good news of the Hereafter, which is Paradise. What is the good news of this world?" He said: "The good dream that the servant sees, or that is seen for him. It is one part of forty-six parts, or seventy parts, of prophethood."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/132).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Bahz told us, Hammad told us, Abu Imran told us, from Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, that he said: "O Messenger of God, a man does a deed and people praise him for it and commend him for it." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "That is the immediate good news of the believer." Narrated by Muslim.[[Musnad Ahmad (5/156) and Sahih Muslim no. (2642).]]

Ahmad also said: Hasan (meaning al-Ashyab) told us, Ibn Lahi'a told us, Darraj told us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, that he said regarding: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾: "The good dream, which the believer is given as good news, is one part of forty-nine parts of prophethood. Whoever sees that, let him inform of it. Whoever sees other than that, it is only from Satan to grieve him. Let him spit to his left three times, say *Allahu akbar*, and not tell anyone of it." The compilers did not record it.[[Musnad Ahmad (2/219). Ibn Lahi'a and Darraj are weak narrators.]]

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, that Darraj Abu al-Samh told him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, that he said: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾: "The good dream, which the believer is given as good news, is one part of forty-six parts of prophethood."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/139).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim al-Mu'addib told me, Ammar ibn Muhammad told us, al-A'mash told us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾. He said: "In this world it is the good dream, which the servant sees or that is seen for him, and in the Hereafter it is Paradise."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/131).]]

Then he narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, from Abu Hasin, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, that he said: "The good dream is good news from God, and it is one of the bringers of good news."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/130). He narrated it in this way as a *mawquf* (stopping at the Companion).]]

Similarly, he narrated it as a *mawquf* report in this way.

He also said: Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Bakr told us, Hisham told us, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The good dream is the good news. The Muslim sees it, or it is seen for him."[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/130).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Hammad al-Dulabi told me, Sufyan told us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, from his father, from Siba' ibn Thabit, from Umm Kurz al-Ka'biyya, who said: "I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'Prophethood has gone, but the bringers of good news remain.'"[[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/133). Ibn Majah narrated it in al-Sunan no. (3896) through Harun al-Hammal, from Sufyan, similarly. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/212): "This chain is sound, its narrators are trustworthy," though Abu Zayd was declared trustworthy only by Ibn Hibban, and only his son narrated from him.]]

Thus it was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayra, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, that they interpreted this as the good dream.

It was also said: What is meant by this is the good news given by the angels to the believer at the time of his death of Paradise and forgiveness, as in the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is God," and then remain steadfast—the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you request, as a welcome from a Forgiving, Merciful One."﴾ [Fussilat: 30–32]

In the hadith of al-Bara': "When the believer is near death, angels with bright faces and white garments come to him and say: 'Come out, O good soul, to rest and fragrance, and a Lord who is not angry.' So the soul comes out of his mouth like a drop flowing from the mouth of a waterskin."

And as for their good news in the Hereafter, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They will not be grieved by the greatest terror, and the angels will receive them, [saying], "This is your day, which you were promised."﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 103]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day you will see the believing men and believing women, their light running before them and at their right hands, [and it will be said], "Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally. That is the great achievement."﴾ [Al-Hadid: 12]. [[In T: "And that is the great achievement."]]
* *
His saying: ﴿There is no alteration of the words of Allah﴾ means: this promise cannot be changed, cannot be broken, and cannot be altered, but is rather established, fixed, and certain to occur: ﴿That is the great achievement.﴾ [[In T: "And that" — which is an error.]]

Allah says to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And let not their saying grieve you﴾ — the saying of these polytheists — "and seek help from Allah against them, and put your trust in Him; for indeed, all honour belongs to Allah," i.e., all of it belongs to Him, to His Messenger, and to the believers. ﴿He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, i.e., He hears the words of His servants and knows their conditions. [[In manuscript T: "and they take lesson."]]

Ibn Kathir said, rebuking those who claimed that Allah has a son: ﴿Glory be to Him! He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani)﴾, meaning: He is exalted above that. He is independent of everything other than Himself, and everything is in need of Him. ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, meaning: how could He have a son from among His creation, when everything is owned by Him and is His servant? ﴿You have no authority for this﴾, meaning: you have no evidence for what you say, which is falsehood and slander! ﴿Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ This is a denunciation, a firm warning, and a severe threat, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." You have certainly produced something monstrous. The heavens nearly rupture from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. Allah, the Exalted, says: Then after Nuh (Noah) We sent Messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs, i.e., with arguments, evidences and demonstrations of the truth of what they had brought them. ﴿So they were not going to believe in what they had denied before﴾, i.e., the nations were not going to believe in what their Messengers brought them, because of their denial of them at the very first time they were sent to them, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sights away, as they did not believe in it the first time﴾ [al-An'am: 110].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors﴾, i.e., just as Allah sealed the hearts of these people, so they did not believe because of their earlier denial, so Allah seals the hearts of those who resemble them among those who came after them, and sets a seal upon their hearts, so they do not believe until they see the painful punishment.

The meaning is that Allah, the Exalted, destroyed the nations that denied the Messengers and saved (wa anja) those who believed in them, and this was after Nuh, peace be upon him. For people, from the time of Adam, peace be upon him, until before him, were upon Islam, until people innovated the worship of idols, so Allah sent Nuh, peace be upon him, to them. This is why the believers will say to him on the Day of Resurrection: "You are the first Messenger whom Allah sent to the people of the earth."

Ibn Abbas said: Between Adam and Nuh there were ten generations (qurun), all of them upon Islam.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed after Nuh? And your Lord is sufficient as Knower and Seer of the sins of His servants﴾ [al-Isra': 17]. In this there is a great warning for the polytheists of the Arabs who denied the chief of the Messengers and the seal of the prophets and messengers. For if those who denied those Messengers were struck by the punishment and retribution that Allah, the Exalted, mentioned, then what do these people think, when they have committed something greater than those did?

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Then We sent﴾ after those messengers ﴿Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾, meaning his people. ﴿With Our signs﴾, meaning Our proofs and evidences. ﴿But they were arrogant, and they were a criminal people﴾, meaning they were too proud to follow the truth and submit to it. ﴿So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Indeed, this is evident magic."﴾ It is as though they swore to this, while knowing that what they said was a lie and a falsehood, may Allah curse them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and haughtiness. So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾ [An-Naml: 14].

﴿He said﴾, meaning Moses said to them, rebuking them: ﴿"Do you say of the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' And magicians do not succeed."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away﴾, meaning to divert us, ﴿from that upon which we found our fathers﴾, meaning the religion they were upon, ﴿and that you two may have the grandeur﴾, meaning you and Aaron may have the greatness and leadership, ﴿in the land? We are not believers in you two."﴾

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Allah the Exalted often mentions the story of Moses, peace be upon him, with Pharaoh in His Mighty Book, because it is among the most wondrous of stories. Pharaoh was extremely wary of Moses, yet destiny ordained that he raised, on his own bed and at his own table like a son, the very one he was wary of. Then he grew up, and Allah arranged a cause that took him out from among them, granted him prophethood, messengership and direct speech, and sent him to Pharaoh to invite him to Allah the Exalted, so that he would worship Him and return to Him. This was despite Pharaoh's great kingdom and authority. Moses came to him with the message of Allah, and he had no minister except his brother Aaron, peace be upon him. Pharaoh rebelled and was arrogant, and zealotry and the wicked, defiant soul seized him. He stiffened his neck, turned away with his strength, claimed what was not his, acted insolently toward Allah, transgressed, oppressed, and humiliated the party of faith from the Children of Israel. Allah the Exalted protected His messenger Moses and his brother Aaron, surrounded them with His care, and guarded them with His eye that does not sleep. Argument, debate and signs continued to appear at the hands of Moses, one after another and time after time, in a way that dazzles minds and bewilders intellects, something nothing can withstand and which no one brings except one supported by Allah. ﴿And no sign do We show them except that it is greater than its sister﴾. Pharaoh and his chiefs, may Allah curse them, persisted in denying all of this, with obstinacy, defiance and stubbornness, until Allah brought upon them His irresistible might and drowned them all in a single cry. ﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-An'am: 45].

﴿He said﴾, meaning Moses said to them, rebuking them: ﴿"Do you say of the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' And magicians do not succeed."﴾ ﴿They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away﴾, meaning to divert us, ﴿from that upon which we found our fathers﴾, meaning the religion they were upon, ﴿and that you two may have the grandeur﴾, meaning you and Aaron may have the greatness and leadership, ﴿in the land? We are not believers in you two."﴾

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Allah the Exalted often mentions the story of Moses, peace be upon him, with Pharaoh in His Mighty Book, because it is among the most wondrous of stories. Pharaoh was extremely wary of Moses, yet destiny ordained that he raised, on his own bed and at his own table like a son, the very one he was wary of. Then he grew up, and Allah arranged a cause that took him out from among them, granted him prophethood, messengership and direct speech, and sent him to Pharaoh to invite him to Allah the Exalted, so that he would worship Him and return to Him. This was despite Pharaoh's great kingdom and authority. Moses came to him with the message of Allah, and he had no minister except his brother Aaron, peace be upon him. Pharaoh rebelled and was arrogant, and zealotry and the wicked, defiant soul seized him. He stiffened his neck, turned away with his strength, claimed what was not his, acted insolently toward Allah, transgressed, oppressed, and humiliated the party of faith from the Children of Israel. Allah the Exalted protected His messenger Moses and his brother Aaron, surrounded them with His care, and guarded them with His eye that does not sleep. Argument, debate and signs continued to appear at the hands of Moses, one after another and time after time, in a way that dazzles minds and bewilders intellects, something nothing can withstand and which no one brings except one supported by Allah. ﴿And no sign do We show them except that it is greater than its sister﴾. Pharaoh and his chiefs, may Allah curse them, persisted in denying all of this, with obstinacy, defiance and stubbornness, until Allah brought upon them His irresistible might and drowned them all in a single cry. ﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-An'am: 45].

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 10, verses 79–82:

Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the story of the magicians with Musa (peace be upon him) in Surah al-A'raf, and the discussion of it has already preceded there. And (it is mentioned) in this surah, in Surah Ta-Ha, and in al-Shu'ara'. That is because Fir'awn (may Allah curse him) wanted to show off before the people and to oppose what Musa (peace be upon him) had brought of the clear truth, with the adornments of magicians and charlatans. So the system was reversed upon him, that aim was not achieved for him, and the divine proofs became manifest in that general assembly. And ﴿the magicians were thrown down prostrate. They said, "We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 46–48]. Fir'awn thought that he could seek help from the sorcerer against the Messenger of the Knower of secrets, but he failed, lost the Garden, and deserved the Fire.

﴿Fir'awn said, "Bring me every learned sorcerer." And when the magicians came, Musa said to them, "Throw what you are going to throw."﴾ Musa said this to them because they had been gathered, and Fir'awn had promised them nearness and great reward. ﴿They said, "O Musa, either you throw first or we will be the first to throw." He said, "Rather, you throw."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 65, 66]. So Musa wanted the initiative to be theirs, so that the people would see what they had done, and then he would bring the truth after them, and it would crush their falsehood. For this reason, when ﴿they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people, frightened them, and brought a great magic﴾ [al-A'raf: 116], ﴿Musa felt a fear within himself. We said, "Do not fear; indeed you are the superior. And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is only the plot of a sorcerer, and the sorcerer does not succeed wherever he comes."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 67–69]. At that point, when they had thrown, Musa said: ﴿"What you have brought is magic. Indeed, Allah will render it void. Indeed, Allah does not allow the work of corrupters to succeed. And Allah will establish the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it."﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar ibn al-Harith narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman (i.e., al-Dashtaki) narrated to us, Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from Layth (i.e., Ibn Abi Sulaym), who said: It has reached me that these verses are a cure for magic by the permission of Allah, the Exalted. They are recited into a vessel containing water, and then it is poured over the head of the one afflicted by magic: the verse from Surah Yunus, ﴿So when they threw, Musa said, "What you have brought is magic. Indeed, Allah will render it void. Indeed, Allah does not allow the work of corrupters to succeed. And Allah will establish the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it."﴾ and the other verse, ﴿So the truth took place, and what they had been doing was voided﴾ [al-A'raf: 118–122], and His saying, ﴿What they have made is only the plot of a sorcerer, and the sorcerer does not succeed wherever he comes﴾ [Ta-Ha: 69].

Allah informs that none believed in Musa (peace be upon him), despite the clear signs, the decisive proofs and the manifest evidences that he brought, except a few of the people of Fir'awn, from among the dhurriyyah (offspring) — and they were the young men — fearing with trepidation and dread of him and of his chiefs, that they would turn them back to what they had been upon of disbelief. This is because Fir'awn was a tyrant, obstinate, extravagant in rebellion and arrogance, and he had power and awe, so that his subjects feared him with an intense fear.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿So none believed in Musa except some offspring of his people, out of fear of Fir'awn and their chiefs, that he would persecute them﴾. He said: The offspring who believed in Musa were from people other than the Children of Isra'il, from the people of Fir'awn, and they were few. Among them were the wife of Fir'awn, the believer of the family of Fir'awn, the treasurer of Fir'awn, and the wife of his treasurer.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying ﴿So none believed in Musa except some offspring of his people﴾ that he said: the Children of Isra'il.

And from Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak and Qatadah: (dhurriyyah) means: the few.

Mujahid said concerning His saying ﴿except some offspring of his people﴾: he said, the Children of Isra'il. He said: they were the descendants of those to whom Musa was sent, after a long time, and their fathers had died.

Ibn Jarir preferred the view of Mujahid regarding the dhurriyyah, that they were from the Children of Isra'il and not from the people of Fir'awn, because the pronoun refers to the nearest previously mentioned party.

But this is open to scrutiny, because the intended meaning of dhurriyyah is the youths and young men, and that they were from the Children of Isra'il. Yet it is well known that all the Children of Isra'il believed in Musa (peace be upon him), rejoiced in him, and knew his description and attributes and the good news of him from their earlier scriptures, and that Allah, exalted is He, would deliver them through him from the captivity of Fir'awn and make them victorious over him. Therefore, when this reached Fir'awn, he took every precaution, but it availed him nothing. When Musa came, Fir'awn inflicted upon them the most severe harm, and they said: ﴿We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us.' He said: 'It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and see how you will act﴾ [al-A'raf: 129]. Given this established, how could the intended meaning be "except some offspring of the people of Musa," who are the Children of Isra'il?

﴿out of fear of Fir'awn and their chiefs﴾, i.e., and the nobles of their people, that he would persecute them. There was none among the Children of Isra'il whom they feared would tempt them away from faith except Qarun, for he was from the people of Musa, yet he oppressed them, but he was inclined toward Fir'awn, attached to him and clinging to his ropes. As for one who says that the pronoun in His saying ﴿and their chiefs﴾ refers to Fir'awn, and the greatness of the kingdom is due to following him, or that it means omitting "family of" (ali) before Fir'awn and placing the genitive in its position, then he has strayed far, although Ibn Jarir related both views from some grammarians. Among what shows that there was none among the Children of Isra'il except a believer is His saying, exalted is He:

Ibn Kathir said, explaining that Allah the Exalted informs about Musa (Moses) that he said to the Children of Israel: ﴿O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him, if you are Muslims﴾. That is: indeed Allah is sufficient for whoever relies upon Him. ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾ [az-Zumar: 36] and ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ [at-Talaq: 3].

Allah often links worship with reliance (tawakkul), as in His saying: ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾ [Hud: 123]; ﴿Say, He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him and upon Him we have relied﴾ [al-Mulk: 29]; ﴿Lord of the east and the west; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Trustee (wakil)﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 9]. Allah also commanded the believers to say in all their prayers, many times: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5].

The Children of Israel complied with this, and they said: ﴿Upon Allah we have relied. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people﴾. That is: do not let them prevail over us, and do not empower them over us, so that they would think they were empowered only because they were upon the truth while we are upon falsehood, and thus they would be tempted by that. This was narrated from Abu Mijlaz and Abu adh-Duha.

Ibn Abi Najih and others, from Mujahid, said: "Do not punish us at the hands of the people of Pharaoh, nor with a punishment from You, for then the people of Pharaoh would say: 'If they were upon the truth, they would not have been punished, nor would we have been empowered over them,' and so they would be tempted by us."

Abd ar-Razzaq said: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from Ibn Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people﴾, that is: do not empower them over us, for they would then tempt us.

﴿And save us by Your mercy﴾, that is: deliver us by mercy and kindness from You, ﴿from the disbelieving people﴾, that is: those who concealed and covered up the truth, while we have believed in You and relied upon You.

The Almighty mentions the reason for His saving the Children of Israel from Pharaoh and his people, and the manner of their deliverance from them. Allah the Exalted commanded Musa and his brother Harun, peace be upon them both, ﴿that you two should settle﴾, meaning: that they should take for their people in Egypt houses [[In manuscript A: "minhu" (from it).]].

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And make your houses a qiblah (direction of prayer)﴾. Al-Thawri and others related from Khusayf, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: concerning ﴿And make your houses a qiblah﴾, he said: they were commanded to take them as masajid (places of prayer).

Al-Thawri also said, from Ibn Mansur, from Ibrahim: concerning ﴿And make your houses a qiblah﴾, he said: they were fearful, so they were commanded to pray in their houses.

Likewise said Mujahid, Abu Malik, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Dahhak, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and his father Zayd ibn Aslam. It seems, and Allah knows best, that when the affliction from Pharaoh and his people intensified against them and they constrained them, they were commanded to increase their prayer, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 156]. And in the hadith: "When a matter distressed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would pray." Related by Abu Dawud [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1319), from the hadith of Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. For this reason, Allah the Exalted said in this verse: ﴿And make your houses a qiblah, and establish the prayer, and give good tidings to the believers﴾, meaning: with reward and with near victory.

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas, concerning the interpretation of this verse, that he said: The Children of Israel said to Musa, peace be upon him: "We cannot display our prayer in front of the Pharaohs." So Allah the Exalted permitted them to pray in their houses, and they were commanded to make their houses face the qiblah. Mujahid said: ﴿And make your houses a qiblah﴾: When the Children of Israel feared that Pharaoh would kill them in the great churches, they were commanded to make their houses masajid facing the Ka'bah, where they would pray secretly. Qatadah and al-Dahhak said likewise.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿And make your houses a qiblah﴾, meaning: some of them face others.

This is a report from God, Exalted is He, of what Moses, peace be upon him, prayed against Pharaoh and his chiefs, when they refused to accept the truth and persisted in their misguidance and disbelief, opposing and denying out of wrongdoing, arrogance, haughtiness and tyranny. He said: ﴿Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment﴾, that is, of the furnishings and provisions of this world, ﴿and wealth﴾, that is, abundant and plentiful, ﴿in the life of this world. Our Lord, that they may lead [people] astray from Your way﴾ — with the letter yā' pronounced with a fatḥah — meaning: You gave them that, while You know that they will not believe in what You sent me to them with, as a gradual leading on (istidrāj) from You toward them, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿that We may test them therein﴾.

Others read: ﴿li-yuḍillū﴾ with a ḍammah on the yā', meaning: so that by what You have given them, whoever of Your creation You will is tested, so that whoever You have caused to go astray thinks that You gave these people this only out of Your love for them and Your care for them.

﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth﴾. Ibn 'Abbās and Mujāhid said: that is, destroy it. Ḍaḥḥāk, Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Rabī' ibn Anas said: God turned it into carved stones in the form of what they had been.

Qatādah said: We have been told that their crops were turned into stones.

Muḥammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazī said: make their sugar (sukkar) into stones.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Isma'il ibn Abi al-Harith narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Abu Ma'shar, who said: Muhammad ibn Qays narrated to me that Muhammad ibn Ka'b recited Surah Yunus to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz: ﴿And Moses said, "Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿obliterate their wealth﴾ to the end of it. [So 'Umar said to him: "O Abu Hamzah, what is the obliteration (ṭams)?" He said: "All their wealth returned to stone."] Then 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said to a servant of his: "Bring me a bag." [So he brought him a bag.] And in it were chickpeas and eggs, which had been cut around stones.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And harden their hearts﴾, Ibn 'Abbās said: that is, seal them up, ﴿so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾.

This supplication was made by Moses, peace be upon him, out of zeal for God and His religion against Pharaoh and his chiefs, of whom it became clear to him that there was no good in them and nothing would come from them, just as Noah, peace be upon him, prayed, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except a wicked, ungrateful disbeliever﴾ [Nuh 71:26–27]. Therefore God, Exalted is He, answered Moses, peace be upon him, regarding them in this supplication, which his brother Aaron said Amen to. God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Your supplication has been answered, so both of you remain steadfast﴾.

Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Salih, 'Ikrimah, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: Moses supplicated and Aaron said Amen, meaning: We have answered you both in what you asked for regarding the destruction of Pharaoh's family.

Those who argue from this verse say: "The amen of the follower over the recitation of al-Fatihah is considered as if he had recited it, because Moses supplicated and Aaron said Amen."

God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿He said, "Your supplication has been answered, so remain steadfast and do not follow the path of those who do not know"﴾, meaning: just as your supplication has been answered, remain steadfast upon My command.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Ibn 'Abbās: ﴿So remain steadfast﴾ — proceed according to My command, and that is steadfastness. Ibn Jurayj said: They say that Pharaoh remained after this supplication for forty years.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said: forty days.

Ibn Jurayj said, from Ibn 'Abbās: ﴿So remain steadfast﴾ — proceed according to My command, and that is steadfastness. Ibn Jurayj said: They say that Pharaoh remained after this supplication for forty years.

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said: forty days.

He, may He be exalted, mentions the manner in which He drowned Pharaoh and his armies. When the Children of Israel left Egypt in the company of Musa (peace be upon him), and they were, it is said, six hundred thousand fighting men apart from the offspring, and they had borrowed much jewelry from the Copts and carried it with them, Pharaoh's rage against them intensified. He sent heralds (*hashirin*) into the cities to gather his armies from his provinces. He rode after them with great pomp and fearsome hosts, for what Allah, may He be exalted, intended for them. No one who held a position of power or authority in all his kingdom stayed behind. They caught up with them at sunrise. ﴿So when the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said, "We are surely overtaken."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 61]

That was because when they reached the shore of the sea, and Pharaoh had caught up with them, and there was nothing left but for the two hosts to fight [[In A: "that the two hosts meet."]], the companions of Musa (peace be upon him) pressed him with the question: how is the escape from what we are in? He said: "I have been commanded to proceed this way." ﴿"No indeed! My Lord is with me; He will guide me."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 62] So when the matter became constricted, it was widened. Allah, may He be exalted, commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, and he struck it, and the sea split. ﴿So each part was like a huge mountain﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 63], that is, like a great mountain, and it became twelve paths, one for each tribe. Allah commanded the wind, and it dried its ground. ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea, not fearing being overtaken nor being afraid﴾ [Taha: 77]. The water was split between the paths like windows, so that each people could see the others, lest they think that they had perished. The Children of Israel crossed the sea. When the last of them had come out of it, Pharaoh and his armies reached its edge on the other side. He had with him a hundred thousand dark-colored horses, apart from the rest of the colors. When he saw that, it terrified him, he held back, feared, and intended to turn back. But it was too late, and there was no escape. The decree was carried out, and the supplication was answered.

Jibril (peace be upon him) came on a female horse, a mare [*wadiq*] of a dark-brown color [*ha'il*] [[The text reads: "waddīq ḥā'il"; the translation follows the common reading.]], and passed beside Pharaoh's horse, and it neighed toward her. Jibril went ahead and plunged into the sea and entered it, and the horse plunged in behind him. Pharaoh no longer had control over himself. He forced himself before his commanders and said to them: "The Children of Israel have no more right to the sea than we do." So they all plunged in, to the last of them, with Mika'il at their rear, leaving none of them behind without bringing him along. When they had gathered together in it and were complete, and the first of them intended to come out of it, Allah, the All-Powerful, commanded the sea to close over them, and it closed over them. Not one of them was saved. The waves kept lifting them up and bringing them down, and the waves piled up over Pharaoh. The agonies of death overtook him, and while in that state he said: ﴿"I believe that there is no god except He in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am among the submitting ones."﴾ He believed at a time when belief would not benefit him. ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their belief did not benefit them when they saw Our might. [This is] the way of Allah which has already passed among His servants. And there the disbelievers lost.﴾ [Ghafir: 84–85]

Thus Allah, may He be exalted, said in reply to Pharaoh when he said what he said: ﴿"Now? And you had disobeyed before, and were among the corrupters."﴾ That is: is this the time you speak, when you had disobeyed Allah before this, in what was between you and Him? ﴿And you were among the corrupters﴾, that is, on earth, those who led people astray. ﴿And We made them leaders calling to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 41]

What Allah related about Pharaoh in this statement of his, in that state, is one of the secrets of the unseen which Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of. For this reason, the Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Pharaoh said: ﴿I believe that there is no god except He in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾, Jibril said to me: '[O Muhammad], if you had seen me as I took a clot [*hal*] of mud from the sea and stuffed it into his mouth, fearing that mercy would reach him.'" [[Addition from T, A, and the Musnad.]] It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim in their tafsirs, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, with this chain. [[Musnad (1/309) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3107).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: it is a hasan (sound-good) hadith.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah related to us, from Adi ibn Thabit and Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril said to me: 'If you had seen me as I took a clot from the sea and pushed it into the mouth of Pharaoh, fearing that mercy would overtake him.'" This was also related by Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi and by Ibn Jarir, by other routes, from Shu'bah, with it. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3108); Tafsir al-Tabari (15/190–192). al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (2/340) through al-Nadr ibn Shumayl from Shu'bah, and said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, but they did not record it, because most of Shu'bah's companions stopped it at Ibn Abbas." al-Bayhaqi related it in Shu'ab al-Iman no. (9392), mentioning the narrations that are marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and mawquf (stopped at Ibn Abbas).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan, gharib, sahih.

In a narration in Ibn Jarir, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Ata and Adi, from Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas, one of them traced it to the Prophet, and it seems the other did not trace it. Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar related to us, from Umar ibn Abd Allah ibn Ya'la al-Thaqafi, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah drowned Pharaoh, he pointed with his finger and raised his voice: ﴿"I believe that there is no god except He in whom the Children of Israel believe"﴾. He said: Jibril feared that Allah's mercy would precede His wrath toward him, so he began to take a clot with his wings and strike it into his face and stuff it in.

Ibn Jarir related it similarly from Sufyan ibn Wakee, from Abu Khalid, with it, as a mawquf (stopped at Ibn Abbas) report. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/193). al-Sarqusti related it in Gharib al-Hadith, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/138), from Musa ibn Harun, from Yahya al-Hammani, from Abu Khalid al-Ahmar, with similar wording.]]

It has also been related from a hadith of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Humayd related to us: Hakkam related to us, from Anbasah — that is, Ibn Sa'id — from Kathir ibn Zadhan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril said to me: 'O Muhammad, if you had seen me as I was pressing it down and stuffing clay [*al-hal*] into his mouth, fearing that the mercy of Allah would reach him and He would forgive him.'" He means: Pharaoh. [[In T: "al-jibal" (the mountains).]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/191); al-Bayhaqi related it in Shu'ab al-Iman no. (9390) through Hakkam al-Razi.]]

Regarding this Kathir ibn Zadhan, Ibn Ma'in said: "I do not know him." Abu Zur'ah and Abu Hatim said: "Unknown (majhul)," while the rest of its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat).

A group of the early generations (al-salaf, the pious predecessors) also related this hadith in mursal form: Qatadah, Ibrahim al-Taymi, and Maymun ibn Mihran. It is also reported from al-Dahhak ibn Qays that he delivered a sermon to the people with this. Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: ﴿So today We will save you in your body, so that you may be a sign for those who come after you.﴾ Ibn Abbas and others from the early generations said: Some of the Children of Israel doubted the death of Pharaoh, so Allah, may He be exalted, commanded the sea to cast him up with his body, without a soul, wearing his well-known armor, onto a raised place of the earth [*najwah*], so that they could be certain of his death and destruction. For this reason, He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So today We will save you﴾, that is, We will raise you on a height [*nashz*] of the earth. ﴿In your body.﴾ Mujahid said: "In your body." al-Hasan said: "In a body with no soul in it." Abd Allah ibn Shaddad said: "Intact and whole," that is, not torn, so that they could verify him and recognize him. Abu Sakhr said: "In your armor."

All these statements are not contradictory, as has been mentioned previously. Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: ﴿so that you may be a sign for those who come after you﴾, that is, so that he would be a proof for the Children of Israel of your death and destruction, and that Allah is the Capable, in whose hand is the forelock of every creature, and that nothing can stand against His anger. For this reason, some of the early generations recited: "So that you may be a sign for those who created you" [[In T: "al-ghafilun"; the recitation variant is noted by the editor.]] And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs, that is, they do not take admonition from them, nor do they learn a lesson.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us: Ghundar related to us: Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina, and the Jews were fasting on the day of Ashura. They said: "This is a day on which Musa prevailed over Pharaoh." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "You have more right to Musa than they do, so fast it." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4680).]]
