He said: Jibril feared that Allah's mercy would precede His wrath toward him, so he began to take a clot with his wings and strike it into his face and stuff it in.

Ibn Jarir related it similarly from Sufyan ibn Wakee, from Abu Khalid, with it, as a mawquf (stopped at Ibn Abbas) report. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/193). al-Sarqusti related it in Gharib al-Hadith, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf (2/138), from Musa ibn Harun, from Yahya al-Hammani, from Abu Khalid al-Ahmar, with similar wording.]]

It has also been related from a hadith of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Jarir said:

Ibn Humayd related to us: Hakkam related to us, from Anbasah — that is, Ibn Sa'id — from Kathir ibn Zadhan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril said to me: 'O Muhammad, if you had seen me as I was pressing it down and stuffing clay [*al-hal*] into his mouth, fearing that the mercy of Allah would reach him and He would forgive him.'" He means: Pharaoh. [[In T: "al-jibal" (the mountains).]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/191); al-Bayhaqi related it in Shu'ab al-Iman no. (9390) through Hakkam al-Razi.]]

Regarding this Kathir ibn Zadhan, Ibn Ma'in said: "I do not know him." Abu Zur'ah and Abu Hatim said: "Unknown (majhul)," while the rest of its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat).

A group of the early generations (al-salaf, the pious predecessors) also related this hadith in mursal form: Qatadah, Ibrahim al-Taymi, and Maymun ibn Mihran. It is also reported from al-Dahhak ibn Qays that he delivered a sermon to the people with this. Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: ﴿So today We will save you in your body, so that you may be a sign for those who come after you.﴾ Ibn Abbas and others from the early generations said: Some of the Children of Israel doubted the death of Pharaoh, so Allah, may He be exalted, commanded the sea to cast him up with his body, without a soul, wearing his well-known armor, onto a raised place of the earth [*najwah*], so that they could be certain of his death and destruction. For this reason, He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So today We will save you﴾, that is, We will raise you on a height [*nashz*] of the earth. ﴿In your body.﴾ Mujahid said: "In your body." al-Hasan said: "In a body with no soul in it." Abd Allah ibn Shaddad said: "Intact and whole," that is, not torn, so that they could verify him and recognize him. Abu Sakhr said: "In your armor."

All these statements are not contradictory, as has been mentioned previously. Allah knows best.

* *

His statement: ﴿so that you may be a sign for those who come after you﴾, that is, so that he would be a proof for the Children of Israel of your death and destruction, and that Allah is the Capable, in whose hand is the forelock of every creature, and that nothing can stand against His anger. For this reason, some of the early generations recited: "So that you may be a sign for those who created you" [[In T: "al-ghafilun"; the recitation variant is noted by the editor.]] And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs, that is, they do not take admonition from them, nor do they learn a lesson.

The destruction of Pharaoh and his chiefs was on the day of Ashura, as al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us: Ghundar related to us: Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina, and the Jews were fasting on the day of Ashura. They said: "This is a day on which Musa prevailed over Pharaoh." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "You have more right to Musa than they do, so fast it." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4680).]]

He, may He be exalted, mentions the manner in which He drowned Pharaoh and his armies. When the Children of Israel left Egypt in the company of Musa (peace be upon him), and they were, it is said, six hundred thousand fighting men apart from the offspring, and they had borrowed much jewelry from the Copts and carried it with them, Pharaoh's rage against them intensified. He sent heralds (*hashirin*) into the cities to gather his armies from his provinces. He rode after them with great pomp and fearsome hosts, for what Allah, may He be exalted, intended for them. No one who held a position of power or authority in all his kingdom stayed behind. They caught up with them at sunrise. ﴿So when the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said, "We are surely overtaken."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 61]

That was because when they reached the shore of the sea, and Pharaoh had caught up with them, and there was nothing left but for the two hosts to fight [[In A: "that the two hosts meet."]], the companions of Musa (peace be upon him) pressed him with the question: how is the escape from what we are in? He said: "I have been commanded to proceed this way." ﴿"No indeed! My Lord is with me; He will guide me."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 62] So when the matter became constricted, it was widened. Allah, may He be exalted, commanded him to strike the sea with his staff, and he struck it, and the sea split. ﴿So each part was like a huge mountain﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 63], that is, like a great mountain, and it became twelve paths, one for each tribe. Allah commanded the wind, and it dried its ground. ﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea, not fearing being overtaken nor being afraid﴾ [Taha: 77]. The water was split between the paths like windows, so that each people could see the others, lest they think that they had perished. The Children of Israel crossed the sea. When the last of them had come out of it, Pharaoh and his armies reached its edge on the other side. He had with him a hundred thousand dark-colored horses, apart from the rest of the colors. When he saw that, it terrified him, he held back, feared, and intended to turn back. But it was too late, and there was no escape. The decree was carried out, and the supplication was answered.

Jibril (peace be upon him) came on a female horse, a mare [*wadiq*] of a dark-brown color [*ha'il*] [[The text reads: "waddīq ḥā'il"; the translation follows the common reading.]], and passed beside Pharaoh's horse, and it neighed toward her. Jibril went ahead and plunged into the sea and entered it, and the horse plunged in behind him. Pharaoh no longer had control over himself. He forced himself before his commanders and said to them: "The Children of Israel have no more right to the sea than we do." So they all plunged in, to the last of them, with Mika'il at their rear, leaving none of them behind without bringing him along. When they had gathered together in it and were complete, and the first of them intended to come out of it, Allah, the All-Powerful, commanded the sea to close over them, and it closed over them. Not one of them was saved. The waves kept lifting them up and bringing them down, and the waves piled up over Pharaoh. The agonies of death overtook him, and while in that state he said: ﴿"I believe that there is no god except He in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am among the submitting ones."﴾ He believed at a time when belief would not benefit him. ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their belief did not benefit them when they saw Our might. [This is] the way of Allah which has already passed among His servants. And there the disbelievers lost.﴾ [Ghafir: 84–85]

Thus Allah, may He be exalted, said in reply to Pharaoh when he said what he said: ﴿"Now? And you had disobeyed before, and were among the corrupters."﴾ That is: is this the time you speak, when you had disobeyed Allah before this, in what was between you and Him? ﴿And you were among the corrupters﴾, that is, on earth, those who led people astray. ﴿And We made them leaders calling to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 41]

What Allah related about Pharaoh in this statement of his, in that state, is one of the secrets of the unseen which Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of. For this reason, the Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Sulayman ibn Harb related to us: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Pharaoh said: ﴿I believe that there is no god except He in whom the Children of Israel believe﴾, Jibril said to me: '[O Muhammad], if you had seen me as I took a clot [*hal*] of mud from the sea and stuffed it into his mouth, fearing that mercy would reach him.'" [[Addition from T, A, and the Musnad.]] It was also related by al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim in their tafsirs, from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, with this chain. [[Musnad (1/309) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3107).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: it is a hasan (sound-good) hadith.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'bah related to us, from Adi ibn Thabit and Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril said to me: 'If you had seen me as I took a clot from the sea and pushed it into the mouth of Pharaoh, fearing that mercy would overtake him.'" This was also related by Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi and by Ibn Jarir, by other routes, from Shu'bah, with it. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3108); Tafsir al-Tabari (15/190–192). al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (2/340) through al-Nadr ibn Shumayl from Shu'bah, and said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, but they did not record it, because most of Shu'bah's companions stopped it at Ibn Abbas." al-Bayhaqi related it in Shu'ab al-Iman no. (9392), mentioning the narrations that are marfu' (traced to the Prophet) and mawquf (stopped at Ibn Abbas).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan, gharib, sahih.

They said: "This is a day on which Musa prevailed over Pharaoh." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "You have more right to Musa than they do, so fast it." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4680).]]

Ibn Kathir said: Allah the Exalted informs of the blessings He bestowed upon the Children of Israel, both religious and worldly. As for ﴿a good abode﴾ [[In manuscript T: "fa-al-mubawwa'"]], it was said that it refers to the lands of Egypt and the Levant, namely the areas adjoining Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and its surroundings. When Allah the Exalted destroyed Pharaoh and his armies, the rule of the Mosaic state became firmly established over all of the land of Egypt, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We caused to inherit the people who had been oppressed the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of what they endured patiently. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been constructing and what they had been erecting﴾ [al-A'raf: 137]. And He said in another verse: ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs, and treasures and a noble station. Thus [it was]. And We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them﴾ [ash-Shu'ara: 57-59] [[In manuscripts T and A: "how much they left of gardens, springs and crops."]].

However, they continued with Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, seeking the land of Bayt al-Maqdis [and this is the land of al-Khalil (Abraham), peace be upon him, so Musa continued with those who were with him seeking Bayt al-Maqdis] [[Addition from T and A.]]. In it there was a people from the Amalekites, [so the Children of Israel shrank back from fighting the Amalekites] [[Addition from T and A.]], and so Allah the Exalted scattered them in the wilderness of al-Tih for forty years. Harun (Aaron) died there, then Musa, peace be upon them both [[In A: "during those years."]], and after them they set out with Yusha' ibn Nun (Joshua son of Nun), and Allah opened Bayt al-Maqdis to them, and their hands remained over it until Bukhtansar (Nebuchadnezzar) seized it from them for a period of time. Then it returned to them, and then the kings of the Greeks (Yunan) took it, and it remained under their rule for a long period. During that period Allah sent 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary), peace be upon him. The Jews sought help from the kings of the Greeks, who ruled over them, in opposing 'Isa, peace be upon him. They informed on him to them and suggested to them that this man would corrupt your subjects. So they sent someone to arrest him, but Allah raised him to Himself. Some of the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) were made to resemble him by the will and decree of Allah [[In A: "and His power."]], so they seized him and crucified him, and believed that he was 'Isa. ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them. And indeed those who differed over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they certainly did not kill him. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself. And Allah is ever Exalted in might and Wise﴾ [an-Nisa': 157-158].

Then, about three hundred years after the Messiah, peace be upon him, Constantine, one of the kings of the Greeks, entered the religion of Christianity, and he had been a philosopher before that. It is said that he entered the Christian religion out of dissimulation (taqiyyah), and it is said that it was a ruse to corrupt it. The bishops (asaqifah) among them laid down for him laws, a code, and innovations which they introduced. He built for them churches and great and small houses of worship, monasteries, sanctuaries, temples and cells. Christianity spread in that era and became famous, despite what it contained of alteration, change, distortion, fabrication, falsehood, and opposition to the religion of the Messiah. Among them there remained, upon the true religion of the Messiah, only a few monks, who took for themselves monasteries in the deserts, wastelands and barren lands. The hand of the Christians took hold of the kingdom of al-Sham, al-Jazirah and the lands of the Romans. This aforementioned king built the city of Constantinople, al-Qumamah, Bayt Lahm (Bethlehem), and churches in the lands of Bayt al-Maqdis, and the cities of Hawran such as Busra and others among the lands, with enormous and sturdy structures. From that time they worshipped the cross, prayed facing the east, painted the churches (with images), and made the flesh of swine lawful, and other things they introduced of branches and roots into their religion. They also devised for it the lowly confession which they call the Great [confession], and they composed for it codes of law.

But to expound on this would take long.

The point is that their hand remained over these lands until the Companions (al-Sahabah, the Prophet's companions), may Allah be pleased with them, wrested them from their hands. The conquest of Bayt al-Maqdis took place at the hands of the Commander of the Believers, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and all praise and favour belong to Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾, meaning the lawful, from good provision, beneficial and pleasant both by nature and by Shari'ah (sacred law).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they did not differ until knowledge came to them﴾, meaning they did not differ on any of the matters except after knowledge had come to them, that is, it was not for them to differ, and Allah had made it clear to them and removed confusion from them. It has been related in a hadith (prophetic tradition) that the Jews split into seventy-one sects, that the Christians split into seventy-two sects, and that this Ummah (community) will split into seventy-three sects, one of which is in Paradise and seventy-two in the Fire. It was asked: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Those who are upon what I and my Companions are upon."

Al-Hakim related it in his al-Mustadrak with this wording, and it is in the Sunan and the Masanid [[al-Mustadrak (1/129) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As; it also came from the hadiths of Mu'awiyah, Anas and 'Awf ibn Malik. al-Iraqi said: "Its chains are sound."]].

And for this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them﴾, meaning He will decide between them, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾.

Qatadah ibn Di'amah said: "It has reached us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'I do not doubt, and I do not ask.'" [Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (15/202) from Ma'mar from Qatadah, as a mursal report.]

Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan al-Basri said the same. This contains a confirmation (tathbit) for the community, and an informing of them that the description of their Prophet ﷺ is present in the earlier scriptures that are in the hands of the People of the Book, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet, the unlettered, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel...﴾ [al-A'raf: 157] to the end of the verse. Then, despite this knowledge, they recognise him from their books as they recognise their own sons; they conceal it, distort it and alter it, and they do not believe in him despite the establishment of proof against them. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ That is, they will not believe with a faith that benefits them, but only when faith will no longer benefit a soul. For this reason, when Musa, peace be upon him, invoked against Pharaoh and his chiefs, he said: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 88], as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered against them every thing before them, they would not have believed unless Allah willed; but most of them are ignorant.﴾ [al-An'am: 111] Then Allah, the Exalted, said:

Allah says: "Why was there not a town that believed in its entirety from among the earlier nations to whom We sent messengers? Rather, no messenger did We send before you, O Muhammad, except that his people denied him, or most of them," as Allah said: ﴿Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them except that they mock him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 30], ﴿Thus did no messenger come to those before them except that they said: "A sorcerer or a madman!"﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 52], ﴿And thus did We not send before you a warner into a town except that its affluent ones said: "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps"﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 23] [[In T: "Wa ma arsalna fi qaryatin min nabiyy" (And We did not send in a town a prophet).]] [[In T: "muhtadun" (guided), which is an error.]]

And in the authentic hadith: "The prophets were shown to me. A prophet would pass by with a group of people (fi'am) of men, a prophet would pass with two men, and a prophet with no one with him at all." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (5752), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (220), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.]] Then he mentioned the large number of the followers of Musa, peace be upon him, then he mentioned the large number of his own ummah, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, a multitude that filled the two horizons, the east (ash-Sharqi) and the west (al-Gharbi).

The point is that no town from among the earlier towns was found to have believed in its entirety along with its prophet, except the people of Yunus, who were the people of Nineveh (Ninawa). Their faith was only out of fear of the arrival of the punishment with which their messenger had warned them, after they saw its signs and their messenger had departed from among them. Then they cried out to Allah, sought refuge in Him, humbled themselves before Him, submitted, brought their children, their animals and their livestock, and asked Allah the Exalted to remove from them the punishment with which their prophet had warned them. Then Allah had mercy on them, lifted the punishment from them, and they were given respite, as Allah said: ﴿Except the people of Yunus: when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and let them enjoy for a time﴾.

The commentators differed: Was the punishment of the Hereafter lifted from them along with the worldly punishment, or was it lifted only in this world? There are two opinions. One is that it was only in the life of this world, as is restricted in this verse. The second opinion, in their favour, is based on the saying of Allah: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more, and they believed, so We let them enjoy for a time﴾ [as-Saffat: 147-148]. He ascribed faith to them, and faith saves from the punishment of the Hereafter. This is the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best.

Qatadah said in explaining this verse: "No town that disbelieved and then believed when the punishment came upon it benefited, and so it was left alone, except the people of Yunus. When they lost their prophet and thought that the punishment had drawn near to them, Allah cast repentance into their hearts. They wore coarse woollen garments (al-musuh), separated every beast from its young, then they wailed to Allah for forty nights. When Allah knew from them the sincerity of their hearts, their repentance and their regret for what had passed from them, Allah removed the punishment from them after it had hung over them." Qatadah said: "It is mentioned that the people of Yunus were in Nineveh, the land of Mosul."

Similarly it was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and other than one of the early generations. Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it: "Fa-halla kanat qaryatun amanat" (Why was there not a town that believed).

Abu Imran narrated from Abu al-Jald, who said: "When the punishment came down upon the people of Yunus, it began to revolve over their heads like pieces of the dark night. They went to a man from among their scholars and said: 'Teach us a supplication with which we may call upon Allah, perhaps He will remove the punishment from us.' He said: 'Say: O Living when there is no living, O Giver of life to the dead, there is no god but You.' He said: So Allah removed the punishment from them."

The complete account will come in detail in Surat as-Saffat, Allah willing.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if your Lord had willed﴾ — O Muhammad — ﴿He would have permitted all the people of the earth to believe in what you have brought them, and they would all have believed.﴾ But He has wisdom in what He does, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one nation, but they continue to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."﴾ [Hud: 118, 119]. He also said: ﴿Have not those who believed despaired that, if Allah willed, He could guide mankind entirely?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 31]. For this reason, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Would you then compel the people﴾, meaning: would you force them and compel them, ﴿until they become believers?﴾, meaning: this is not upon you, nor is it in your hands; rather, [it is] [[Addition from manuscript T.]] with Allah. ﴿He sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let your soul go to waste in grief over them﴾ [Fatir: 8]. ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 272]. ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they will not be believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3]. ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like﴾ [al-Qasas: 56]. ﴿So your duty is only to deliver the message, and upon Us is the account﴾ [al-Ra'd: 40]. ﴿So remind, for you are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 21, 22], and other verses that indicate that Allah the Exalted is the one who does what He wills, who guides whom He wills, and who sends astray whom He wills, by His knowledge, His wisdom and His justice. For this reason He said: ﴿It is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah, and He places defilement﴾ [[In T: "yu'min" (he believes).]] — which is ruin ([[In T: "al-Jibal".]] al-Khabal) — and error, ﴿upon those who do not reason﴾, meaning: the proofs of Allah and His evidences. He is the Just in all of that: in guiding whom He guides, and in misguiding whom He misguides.

The Almighty directs His servants to reflect upon His favours and upon what He has created in the heavens and the earth, which are signs that astonish people of understanding. These include the shining stars, both fixed and wandering, the sun and the moon, the night and the day, their alternation, and the way each one enters the other, so that this one lengthens while that one shortens, and then that one shortens while this one lengthens. They also include the height and vastness of the sky, its beauty and adornment, and the rain that Allah sends down from it, by which He gives life to the earth after its death. Through it He brings forth various fruits, crops, flowers and kinds of plants, and the many creatures of different shapes, colours and benefits that He has scattered upon it. They include the mountains, plains and deserts, the inhabited and the ruined places. They also include the wonders of the sea and its waves. Yet despite all this, it is subjugated and made submissive to those who travel upon it. It carries their ships and runs with them gently, by the power of the All-Powerful who subjected it to them. There is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe.﴾ That is: what benefit do the heavenly and earthly signs, and the messengers with their signs, their proofs and their evidences that indicate their truthfulness, bring to a people who do not believe? This is as He said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 96, 97]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then do they await anything but like the days of those who passed on before them?﴾ That is: do these deniers of yours, O Muhammad, await any vengeance and punishment other than like the days of Allah concerning those who passed before them, the nations that denied their messengers? ﴿Say, "Then wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait." Then We will save Our messengers and those who believed.﴾ That is: and We will destroy those who denied the messengers. ﴿Thus it is an obligation upon Us to save the believers.﴾ [Haqqan:] "Haqqan" means that He, the Exalted, made it obligatory upon Himself, His Noble Self, as in His saying: ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy.﴾ [Al-An'am: 12] As is reported in the two Sahihs, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Indeed Allah wrote a book, and it is with Him above the Throne: 'Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath.'" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7554), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2751), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

* *

* *

As for His saying: ﴿If God touches you with harm﴾ to its end, it is an explanation that good and evil, benefit and harm, all return to God, exalted is He, alone; none shares with Him in that. Thus He alone deserves to be worshipped, with no partner.

The hadith master Ibn 'Asakir narrated, in the biography of Safwan ibn Sulaym, by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed me, from 'Isa ibn Musa, from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seek good all your lifetime, and expose yourselves to the breezes of God's mercy, for God has breezes of His mercy, with which He reaches whom He wills of His servants. And ask Him to conceal your faults and to secure your frights."

Al-Suyuti graded it as weak in al-Jami' (al-Jami' al-Saghir).]]

Then he narrated it by way of al-Layth, from 'Isa ibn Musa, from Safwan, from a man of Ashja', from Abu Hurayra, as a marfu' report (one traced directly to the Prophet), with the same wording.

Then he narrated it by way of al-Layth, from 'Isa ibn Musa, from Safwan, from a man of Ashja', from Abu Hurayra, as a marfu' report (one traced directly to the Prophet), with the same wording.

[[Tarikh Dimashq (8/328, manuscript). Ibn Abi al-Dunya narrated it in al-Faraj ba'd al-Shidda, no. 27, by way of Ruwaym ibn Yazid from al-Layth, as a marfu' report. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Shu'ab al-Iman, no. 1123, by way of Yahya ibn Bukayr from al-Layth, as a marfu' report. Al-Bayhaqi said: "This is the preserved version, not the first." The first is the hadith of Anas.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful﴾, that is, to whoever repents to Him and relies upon Him, whatever sin it may be, even polytheism (shirk) itself, for He accepts the repentance of such a person.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Exalted, commands His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to inform the people that what has come to them from Allah is the truth about which there is no doubt or uncertainty. Whoever is guided by it and follows it, the benefit of that following returns to his own self, and whoever strays from it, the harm of that returns upon him. [[In manuscript T: "from that."]] [[In manuscript T: "upon himself."]] [[Addition from manuscripts T and A.]]

﴿And I am not over you a guardian.﴾ That is: I am not appointed over you to make you believers. I am only a warner to you, and guidance is up to Allah, the Exalted.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient﴾, that is: hold fast to what Allah has sent down to you and revealed to you, and be patient with the opposition of those among the people who oppose you. ﴿Until Allah judges﴾, that is: until He decides between you and them. ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾, that is: the best of those who decide, with His justice [[In manuscript T and A: "with His justice."]] and His wisdom.
